Discover.Title: Discover SBE
Discover.Description: Overview: templates, system settings, scene tools and history.
Discover.WelcomeBody:
System Builder Engine lets you build your own game system, without writing code.
Everything starts from a template: you place the sheet's components in it (values, gauges, buttons, lists…). Characters and items are created from that template and follow its changes.
Discover.TemplatesBody:
“Create Actor”, then the “Template” type: this is the workshop where you design the sheet.
Characters are then created with the “Character” type, from a template.
Discover.ImportBody: A template exported from the workshop (.json file) is recreated here: handy to share a system or bring it into another world.
Discover.ItemsBody:
Same principle for items: an item template, then the items created from it.
Their step buttons provide the actions: rolls, damage, effects, sounds.
Discover.SettingsBody: All SBE settings open from this button.
Discover.ManagersBody:
In the system tab, each module has its own window: theme, combat, effects, calendar, merchants, trades, traces, locks…
A module that replaces a Foundry behavior only turns on once it is set up and saved.
Discover.ToolsBody: With the token tools: place a chest or a merchant, start a new day, manage effects, open the calendar and quests, stain or clean traces, see trap zones.
Discover.ClockBody:
The world's time, date, season, moon and weather at a glance.
The module is enabled with the “Calendar, clock and weather” box in the system settings.
Discover.CarouselBody:
During combat, the combatants' portraits scroll by, with their bars and effects.
Here, a sample combat: nothing is created. The carousel is turned on in its settings.
Discover.UndoBody: Every SBE action (damage, purchase, effect…) is recorded here and can be undone by the GM.
Discover.EndHelp: In windows, a pulsing “?” explains a setting on hover. This tour can be restarted from the tour management, in the settings.

Startup.Name: Startup guided tour: don't show it again
Startup.Hint: When checked, the “Discover SBE” tour no longer starts when the world opens (for you only). Uncheck to see it again at each opening.

Build.Title: Building
Build.Description: The template workshop: components, keys and formulas, sharing, step buttons.
Build.IntroBody:
Everything is built in templates: a character template draws the sheet, an item template draws the items.
This tour opens sample templates: nothing is saved.
Build.WorkshopBody: The sheet is drawn here, component by component. The workshop shows the sheet as players will see it.
Build.AddBody:
“+” adds a component: number, gauge, text, checkbox, dropdown, tags, button, slot, container, frame, columns, tab, chart, level, tree…
Drag it by its handle (⠿) to move it.
Build.ComponentBody:
Each component has a key (here “strength”): formulas use it. The sample's defense is computed with “10 + floor(strength / 2)”.
The pencil opens its settings: dice roll, visible if, editable by players, style, tooltip.
Build.ShareBody: “Export” saves the template's structure to a .json file; “Import” brings it back here or into another world.
Build.ItemModelBody: The same workshop for items. The sample has a weight and a “Use” button.
Build.StepsBody:
A button chains steps, without code: add to a value, consume the item, roll, attack, apply an effect, play a media…
Each step reads like a sentence; “Only if” puts it under a condition.
Build.EndBody: To begin: “Create Actor”, “Template” type. Characters and items created from your templates follow their changes.

Combat.Title: Combat
Combat.Description: Attack rules, area templates, hit locations, combat carousel.
Combat.IntroBody: Rules are set once; each weapon uses them through its “Attack” step.
Combat.RulesBody:
Per character template: attack profiles (roll, defense, damage, criticals), the roll window, ties and rounds.
Changing a rule here changes it for every weapon using the profile.
Combat.TemplatesBody:
Area shapes, drawn once and used by area attacks and by areas that stay on the scene. Each piece has its intensity (here, the blast hits fully at the center and half at the edge).
If your world has none yet, these are samples: nothing is saved.
Combat.BodiesBody:
A body and its parts: a hit lands on a part (by dice or aimed), with its multiplier and its protection.
If your world has none yet, these are samples: nothing is saved.
Combat.CarouselBody: The combatants' portraits, the active combatant first. Here, a sample combat: nothing is created.
Combat.CarouselConfigBody:
Display, bars and effects, tooltip, clicks, visibility, theme and buttons.
The carousel is enabled with the “Combat carousel” box in the system settings.
Combat.EndBody: A weapon is set up in its item template: a button with the “Attack” step and the chosen profile.

Effects.Title: Effects
Effects.Description: The effect manager, its scene tool and an item's own effects.
Effects.IntroBody: An effect is a state placed on a character: bonuses and penalties, duration, stacks, damage over turns, token look.
Effects.ManagerBody:
Create your effects; Foundry's conditions are edited the same way.
For each: what it modifies, its duration, its stacks, its triggers, its tiers, its look on the token.
Effects.ToolBody: This tool also opens the effect manager.
Effects.ItemsBody: An item template grants effects to its carrier. In an item's sheet, the “Effects” tab adds its own rules: while equipped or carried, or when a button is used.
Effects.EndBody: A button can also apply or remove an effect with its “Effect” step.

World.Title: The world
World.Description: Time and weather, quests, merchants, chests, trades, locks, traps, traces, vision, languages.
World.IntroBody: What surrounds the characters: passing time, quests, trade, places and what is left there.
World.CalendarBody: Months, weekdays, seasons, moons, and weather types with their sky, their sounds and their effect on the scene.
World.ClockBody:
Time, date, season, moon and weather, for everyone.
The module is enabled with the “Calendar, clock and weather” box in the system settings.
World.NewDayBody: Characters' rest and what comes back every day: merchants restocked, party save…
World.QuestsBody: On-screen tracking of current quests. Quest journals are created in the Journal tab: objectives, rewards, sections per player.
World.MerchantsBody: Currencies, prices, what is sold and bought back, the default shop. A character becomes a merchant from its sheet.
World.PlaceTitle: Chests and merchants on the scene
World.PlaceBody: Place a chest or a merchant directly on the scene.
World.TradesBody: Players trade items and currencies; choose what can be traded.
World.LocksBody: Locked doors and chests: lockpicking, code, hacking, and tool wear.
World.TrapsBody: A placed item can be a trap. This tool shows their areas: trigger in yellow, effect in red.
World.TracesBody: Stains and footprints left by tokens, erased over time or cleaned from the scene tools.
World.VisionBody: What a token sees and detects: on-screen rendering and perception, given by an item, an effect or the sheet.
World.LanguagesBody: A message written in a language can only be read by those who speak it.
World.EndBody: Each module only counts once it is set up: nothing changes in your game until you use it.

Look.Title: Appearance
Look.Description: System theme, character HUD, token bars, pause banner.
Look.IntroBody: Give your system its look: windows, play panels, tokens.
Look.ThemeBody: Dark and light colors, fonts, interface, window dressing and animations, for the whole system. A template can have its own theme.
Look.HudBody: A template's HUD: its entries (menus, rolls, weapons and items, spells, sheet buttons), their layout and their look, with a live preview. Here, the sample template's one.
Look.BarsBody: The bars shown on tokens: shapes, colors, tiers, animations; for all, per template or per token.
Look.PauseBody: Image or video, text, background band, animation and sound while the game is paused.
Look.EndBody: Each window shows a live preview: try things, nothing is kept without “Save”.
Look.PausePreviewBody: This is the banner players see when the GM pauses the game. Here, a preview: the game is not paused.
Look.HudPreviewBody:
The play panel of the selected character: attack with a carried weapon, make a stat roll, cast a spell…
Here, a sample HUD: nothing is created.
Look.BarsPreviewBody: Sample bars on a token of the scene: nothing is saved, they disappear at the next step.

Tools.Title: Tools
Tools.Description: Action history, template checker, “?” help and guided tours.
Tools.IntroBody: What helps the GM keep control of the game and of their templates.
Tools.UndoBody: Every SBE action is recorded. “Go back here” undoes this action and those that followed; “Redo” replays them.
Tools.CheckerBody: Finds broken keys and formulas in templates and settings, and renames a key everywhere at once.
Tools.HelpBody: A pulsing “?” hides an explanation: hover it to read it.
Tools.TourButtonBody: In the header of windows a tour presents: it starts the tour at that window's step.
Tools.ManageBody: Tour management lists every tour, to start or resume them.
Tools.EndBody: “Discover SBE” starts again when the world opens, as long as its “Don't show at startup” box is unchecked.
Tools.DemoBody: A ready-to-play village that shows the system in action. "Install the demo" adds it to the world (you choose which settings it may replace); "Remove the demo" erases it all and puts your settings back.

Relay.Unsure: An action by {player} was in progress for {gm} when they disconnected: check that it went through (it is not replayed, to avoid a duplicate).
Relay.UnsurePlayer: Your last action was in progress when the GM {gm} disconnected: check that it went through, and redo it if not.

Common.NoGM: No GM is connected: this action needs a GM.

Canvas.OrientHint: Move the mouse to orient (wheel: ±1°, Shift+wheel: ±15°) — click to confirm, Escape or right-click to cancel.

Locks.PickSuccess: The lock gives way: picking succeeded!
Locks.PickFailRemaining: Lockpicking failed — {remaining} attempt(s) left before the lock breaks.
Locks.LockJustBroke: The lock just broke: it is permanently jammed!
Locks.RememberAccess: Remember access (code no longer asked after a success)
Locks.WrongCodeAlarm: Wrong code — the alarm goes off!
Locks.DigicodeLocked: The keypad is out of order: too many attempts!
Locks.RefOnlyWorld: Drop a world item (Items tab) or a carried copy.
Locks.ToolWornOut: {name} is worn out: it can no longer be used.
Locks.NoActor: Select your token (or an assigned character) to try.
Locks.KeysHint: A character carrying a copy of one of these keys opens it without a roll.
Locks.PickToolsHint: A carried tool is used from the lock window. Its field with the same key as the roll (for example "lockpicking") is added to that roll.
Locks.HackToolsHint: A carried tool is used from the lock window. Its field with the same key as the roll is added to that roll.
Locks.MenuHint: Wear of lockpicking and hacking tools.
Locks.WearHint: After each lockpicking or hacking roll, the tool used wears down according to the result. A tool without the wear field does not wear down (only "Destroyed" applies).
Locks.WearKeyHint: The item template field used as durability.
Locks.WearTableHint: A stackable tool (single-use picks) loses one copy instead of disappearing.
Locks.ToolRequiredHint: Checked: only one of the tools dropped above can be used. Unchecked: an attempt without a tool is also possible.
Locks.RollWithToolHint: Unchecked: an accepted tool opens without a roll. Checked: the tool is used for the roll (its bonus is added).
Locks.DifficultyHint: Modifier: makes the roll harder (positive) or easier (negative). Fixed value: the roll is compared to this value instead of the field's. Formulas allowed.

Door.ArmoredHint: Ballistic, independent of the lock: when closed, an armored door stops explosions and area templates; a normal door lets them through (thin door).
Door.LockBrokenPick: The lock is broken: it cannot be picked.
Door.DigicodeDead: The keypad is out of order.

Chest.SoundsHint: Played only for the person opening or closing the chest. Leave the file empty for no sound. Remembered for the next chest you place.
Chest.WeightKeyHint: The item template field used as weight.
Chest.SingleAccess: Single access (one character at a time)
Chest.ClickToPlace: Click on the scene to place the chest.
Chest.OnlyGMCreate: Only the GM can create chests.
Chest.DeleteChestConfirm: Permanently delete this chest? Its contents will be lost.
Chest.SelectTokenNear: Select a token first to open the chest.
Chest.MustBeNear: You are too far from the chest to open it.
Chest.AlreadyInUse: The chest is already in use by {name}.
Chest.LockedByGM: Locked by the GM: it cannot be opened.
Chest.LockBrokenOpen: The lock is broken: the chest can no longer be picked.
Chest.DigicodeDeadOpen: The keypad is out of order: the chest stays shut.
Chest.PlayerLockHint: A padlock set by a player: only they (and the GM) can remove it.
Chest.ContentsWiringHint: Contents will activate with the item system (templates → items → copies). This window is ready for it.
Chest.SizeNaturalHint: If neither box is checked, the chest takes the image's own size.
Chest.SvgNeedsSize: An SVG image has no intrinsic size: check “cells” or “pixels” to impose one.
Chest.DropHint: Drag an item (from the sidebar or your sheet) to store it in the chest.
Chest.TemplatesNotDroppable: A template cannot be carried: drag an ITEM created from that template.
Chest.OnlyObjects: Only SBE items can be put in a chest.
Chest.OverWeight: Too heavy: {total} for a limit of {limit}.
Chest.ActionImpossible: Action not possible on the chest.
Chest.MoneyTooLow: Not enough money to share between {n} characters.
Chest.ClickItemHint: click an item to take or give it
Chest.SelectTokenTake: Select your token (or an assigned character) to take.
Chest.GridHint: Columns 0 = auto. Rows 0 = infinite; with a number (and columns), the chest has columns × rows cells and refuses a new item when full.
Chest.SpatialHint: Columns and rows required: each item takes its size in cells (set on the world item).
Chest.NoCurrencyHint: No currency declared: declare them in the “Merchants and currencies” manager.

Template.DeleteBlocked: Deletion blocked: template “{name}” is used by {count} item(s). Delete those items first.
Template.OptDroppableHint: Unchecked: items of this template are never put on the ground (dragging onto the map, "Drop on the ground").
Template.OptPlayerVisibleHint: Unchecked: only the GM sees items of this template (sheets, chests, ground, HUD, merchants). They still count in formulas.
Template.DeleteElWarn: Allowed, but anything pointing at its key will stop finding it — updating your references is up to you.
Template.EmptyHint: Empty template — click + to add your first component.
Template.ElKeyHint: Unique within this template. Editable — updating what points at it is up to you.
Template.NumComputedSoon: Formulas come at their milestone — computed mode will activate here.
Template.SelChoicesHint: One choice per line, in display order.
Template.StyleSoon: The Style tab (colors, sizes, textures…) comes at its milestone — structure first.
Template.KeyInvalid: Invalid key: start with a lowercase letter, then only lowercase letters, digits or _ (no capitals, accents, hyphens or spaces). E.g. force_bonus.
Template.KeyTaken: Key “{key}” is already used in this template.
Template.KeyRenamed: Key renamed “{old}” → “{key}”: remember to update whatever pointed at it.
Template.SelNeedsChoices: A dropdown list needs at least one choice.
Template.ImgSizeHint: Empty = automatic: the image keeps its natural size or proportions.
Template.ElPlayerVisibleHint: Hierarchical: an invisible container hides all its content. The GM always sees everything.
Template.ColumnsCountHint: Reducing the count moves the surplus content into the last column.
Template.DragSameContainer: Drag & drop reorders within the same container (moving across containers comes later).
Template.DeleteElChildren: This component contains other components: all its content will be deleted with it.
Template.ElLabelPh: (optional — the key is used as label)
Template.SepImageHint: Optional: replaces the line with a full-width image (banner, ornament…). Advanced styling comes with the Style tab.
Template.StyleIntro: Everything is optional: anything left empty keeps the theme's style.
Template.StCustomHint: Declarations applied to the component (e.g. border: 2px solid gold;). To reach further, blocks where “&” stands for the component: &:hover { … }, & .sbe-slot-empty-text { … }, &::after { … }, @media (…) { … }. @keyframes and @property are accepted. The style stays on the component: it follows export and import. At your own risk — it's your system.
Template.GaugeThresholdsHint: As % of the maximum: below the low threshold the gauge takes the low color, above the high threshold the high color.
Template.GaugeLowAboveHigh: The low threshold is greater than the high threshold.
Template.NumFormulaHint: Simple JavaScript expression: other fields' keys are the variables — e.g. (damage + bonus) / 2. Computed in dependency order; the field becomes read-only.
Template.NumBonusFormulaHint: Optional, when computed mode is off: the value stays hand-typed and the formula adds a bonus on top. The field shows the TOTAL (which is also what other formulas, charts and rolls see); clicking it brings back the base value for editing — e.g. floor(strength * 0.10).
Template.StBorderHint: The border shows as soon as a color or a thickness is set.
Template.ElLabelIconHint: Shown before the label — everywhere, charts included. Icon (fa-…), emoji, or image path. In SVG charts (radar, lines…), only emojis are displayed.
Template.StChartTickHint: The scale marks (25, 50, 75…). Branch labels and displayed values are set in the Label and Value groups.
Template.StNoBgHint: No background: only the border and the header bar remain visible (background color and texture are ignored).
Template.DescZoneHint: What you build here shows BELOW the items' description text (e.g. compatible ammo, required tools…).
Template.SheetTabHint: Sheet tab name — renamable (the Description tab is not).
Template.DescTextPlaceholder: The description text is written on each item — what you build here shows below it.
Template.DeleteTabConfirm: Delete tab “{name}”? Its {count} component(s) will be deleted with it.
Template.DragIntoSelf: A container cannot be dropped into itself or one of its children.
Template.DragKindRefused: This component type is not accepted in this container (tabs → navigation, buttons → button menu).
Template.FrameBareHint: The frame becomes transparent: only the collapse caret stays visible.
Template.FrameTitlePosHint: Above: the title floats outside the box — border, background and corners apply to the frame body.
Template.FrameCollapsibleHint: Unchecked: the frame always stays open and the caret is hidden (workshop and sheet).
Template.NavSideHint: Vertical orientation only: the bar sits left or right of the content.
Template.TabIconHint: FontAwesome class (e.g. fa-solid fa-star) OR an image path (e.g. systems/my-rpg/icons/sword.svg).
Template.TabTooltipHint: Text shown when hovering the tab.
Template.ColsEqualHint: Columns take the height of the tallest one, and the last component of each column (a frame, for example) stretches to the bottom: two frames side by side end aligned, with no gap below.
Template.ColsWidthsHint: The total stays at 100%: changing one column automatically redistributes the rest across the others (5% minimum each).
Template.MinMaxSubkeysHint: Dynamic bonuses: if a "key_min" or "key_max" key exists on the sheet, its value is added to the base min/max (e.g. str_max = 20 → max 100+20; negative to lower). Also works for gauge max.
Template.FieldWidthHint: Empty = automatic width (the field takes the available space). Otherwise the field is capped at this width — keeps it from eating the whole column.
Template.GaugeSubkeysHint: Dynamic sub-keys: "key_min" / "key_max" add to the bounds, "key_bas" / "key_haut" shift the thresholds (%).
Template.ElPlayerEditableHint: Unchecked: players see the component but its input is locked — only the GM can change the value.
Template.FramePinnedHint: TOP-LEVEL frame only: it stays fixed at the top of the sheet while the rest scrolls. Ideal for a header.
Template.ElSheetHidden: Hidden on the sheet (even for the GM)
Template.ElSheetHiddenHint: The component never shows on the sheet but its key and value remain usable by formulas — ideal for calculation keys (bonuses, thresholds…).
Template.ElVisibleIfHint: Optional. Expression evaluated live on the sheet: the component only shows when it is true — e.g. poison > 0, hp < 10, weapon_equipped. Empty = always visible. The key and its value stay usable by formulas even while the component is hidden. A failing expression hides the component.
Template.KeyReserved: "{key}" is a reserved word of the formula engine — pick another key (e.g. "strength" instead of "for").
Template.ChartAxesHint: One line per entry, format: key : Label : #color. For PICTOGRAMS, the 3rd part is the ICON (emoji, fa-solid fa-… class, or image path) and the icon count = the key's declared max (keep it small, e.g. 0→5). Computed keys work too — everything updates live.
Template.ChartMaxHint: Empty = automatic: uses the declared min/max of the referenced fields (e.g. attributes 0→100); otherwise fits the values. Set to force your own scale.
Template.ChartSizeHint: Radar/pie: diameter. Line/columns: height. Empty = default size.
Template.ChartColorHint: E.g. #b5471f. Empty = theme accent color. The pie uses an automatic palette (or the per-line color).
Template.ChartNeedsAxes: A radar needs at least {n} data entries to be readable (dropped fields + typed lines combined).
Template.ChartNoAxes: Chart: no axes defined (pencil → Axes / series).
Template.ChartPreviewTip: Preview with sample values — on the sheet, your keys take over.
Template.ChartAxes2Hint: One key per line, in the SAME ORDER as the data — drawn dashed (character vs average, before/after…).
Template.ChartDropHint: Drop a field here (number, gauge) — it moves INTO the chart
Template.ChartRemoveAxis: Remove: the field returns to its original location
Template.ChartKindRefused: Only NUMBER fields and GAUGES can feed a chart.
Template.ChartDup: This field is already in the chart.
Template.ChartDeleteReturns: Its fields will NOT be deleted: each returns to its original location.
Template.HtmlCodeHint: Free markup. Live interpolation: {{key}} shows the key's value, {{= formula}} evaluates a formula (e.g. {{= hp < 30 ? "CRITICAL" : "STABLE" }}). Style via the Style tab or the theme's advanced CSS.
Template.HtmlSecurityNote: 🛡 Security: the HTML is sanitized at render time — scripts, iframes and event handlers are stripped automatically. A shared template can NEVER run code on your machine.
Template.TtTextHint: Free text with interpolation: {{key}} shows a value, {{= formula}} computes. Light HTML allowed (sanitized — never executable code). Line breaks preserved.
Template.TtBonusHint: Lists non-zero key_bonus / _min / _max / _bas / _haut sub-keys, green (+) or red (−).
Template.StChartStepHint: Empty = automatic quarters (0-25-50-75-100%). "by value": one mark every N points (30 → 30, 60, 90…). "by %": one mark every N% of the scale. 40 marks maximum.
Template.StChartGridBgHint: Draws the scale lines behind the bars (Bars and Funnel types). Color and thickness follow the grid settings above.
Template.ImgChoicesHint: Upload your images and give each one an icon, a name, or both: the player picks by clicking, never by path. The stored value stays the path, so this field's key can be used elsewhere — as a frame background in particular. No entry = original behavior, the player clicks the image and picks a file.
Template.StBgTextureKeyHint: Accepts a key in braces — e.g. {{portrait}} or folder/{{state}}.webp. The background then follows the player's choice or the character's state, with a single set of components in the frame.
Template.ImgDefaultHint: The starting image. Give it an icon and a name too: it then becomes a choice like the others, and the player can come back to it.
Template.GaugeCritHint: In % of the maximum, above the high threshold: the gauge takes the critical color (overload, alert…). Empty = no critical zone.
Template.GaugeCritBelowHigh: The critical threshold must be above the high threshold.
Template.NumMaxFormulaHint: Optional: a computed maximum (as for a gauge), replacing the entered maximum. The "key_max" subkey is added to it.
Template.NumShowMaxHint: The effective maximum is shown next to the field, like a gauge's text.
Template.ColorHint: The value is "#rrggbb": readable in formulas and by effects ("@key"). White means "no tint" for effect sight and light.
Template.TabVisibleIfHint: Formula read on the item or sheet. False: the tab is not shown (not even to the GM, like components).
Template.NumBonusToneHint: Carried items' share (default): only what the class, equipment, skills (carried…) bring turns the value green or red; the fixed part of the formula (an attribute) stays neutral. Whole bonus: the entire formula colors it. None: the value always stays neutral.
Template.TtBaseHint: Typed number: the "Base: x" line under the tooltip text, above bonuses and penalties.

Objet.NoTemplateHint: Item without a template — create items from a template (“Create an item”).
Objet.NoTemplatesHint: No template yet — create a Template first, it will appear here as “Name (item)”.
Objet.TemplateNewer: A newer version of the template is available.
Objet.Reloaded: Item realigned with the latest template version: values kept, orphan keys purged.
Objet.TemplateMissing: Template not found — the sheet structure cannot be displayed.
Objet.NoFields: The template has no components yet — build it in its workshop.
Objet.NeedsTemplate: Cannot create an item without a template: create a Template first.
Objet.DeleteCascadeTitle: Delete the item and its copies
Objet.DeleteCascadeConfirm: “{name}” has {count} copy(ies) stored in chests. Delete them too? (Never an orphan copy.)

Formula.UnknownKeys: Unknown keys in the formula: {keys}. Allowed — but they will be “undefined” until they exist.

Table.ColumnsHint: Rows are defined here, on the TEMPLATE. Columns and rows are managed directly on the table (header + adds a column, bottom + adds a row).
Table.DeleteColConfirm: Delete column “{label}”? Its cells will be lost.
Table.FreeCellHint: Free column: the value is entered on the item's sheet.
Table.ColKeyHint: Unique within this table — used as a variable by computed columns.
Table.ColKeyTaken: Key “{key}” is already used in this table.
Table.ColLockedHint: Locked column: filled here in the workshop, not editable on the item. Free column: each item enters its value.
Table.ColFormulaHint: Variables: the other columns' keys (row values) and the sheet's field keys.
Table.DimHint: More → automatic columns (col1, col2… to customize afterwards) and empty rows; fewer → trimmed from the end, surplus content lost.
Table.DimColsTrimmed: {count} column(s) removed from the end (content lost).
Table.DimRowsTrimmed: {count} row(s) removed from the end (content lost).

Button.ShowInCtxHint: Checked by default: the action appears when right-clicking the item in the inventory and in the token HUD. Uncheck for a button that only makes sense inside the item sheet.
Button.ChargesKeyHint: A number or gauge field of THIS template (ammo, uses…). Each use decrements it; depletion triggers the at-zero behavior.
Button.OnZeroQty: Remove 1 from the stack (then the item with the last one)
Button.OnZeroHint: What happens when charges reach zero (or on each use if no charges field).
Button.MenuHint: Add sub-buttons directly on the sheet via the + under this button (e.g. Shoot → Jammed → Unjam).
Button.QtyLater: Quantity removal: will be wired with character inventories.
Button.AmountHint: Fixed number OR formula linked to the sheet's fields — keys are the variables (e.g. damage / 2, burst_ammo).
Button.AmountFormulaFail: Amount formula “{formula}”: invalid result — 1 charge removed by default.
Button.AnnounceHint: A "use" card tells what changed: +7 HP, effect applied, item consumed… Rolls and attacks already have their own card.
Button.IconHint: An image (folder) or a font icon: "fa-solid fa-play".

Tags.EntriesHint: One tag per line. Plain text = fixed badge; “@key” = bound badge showing the field's VALUE (dropdown, number… ; checked checkbox = its label).
Tags.TopNote: displayed at the top of the sheet
Tags.HighlightHint: Which tags take the accent color; the others stay plain.
Tags.PlaceHint: Above the header (full width), or inside the header, just above the name.
Tags.PlaceHeader: Inside the header, above the name

Rich.Preview: Rich text — written on each item.
Rich.EditorHint: Always open: you write directly, like a notepad; the text is saved when you click elsewhere.

Slot.FilterTagHint: Accepted if the item has this tag (fixed or linked). Several tags separated by commas: it must have all of them (e.g. “attachment, grip”). Case does not matter.
Slot.ExcludeTagHint: Optional, comma separated: an item carrying one of them is refused (e.g. the general inventory without recipes).
Slot.Excluded: This place refuses this kind of item.
Slot.FilterKeyHint: Accepted if the item's template has a component with this key.
Slot.NeedObject: This slot holds a carried COPY (not a world item).
Slot.NeedModel: This slot references a WORLD ITEM (not a carried copy).
Slot.Rejected: This item does not match the slot's filter.
Slot.Missing: The housed item cannot be found (deleted?).
Slot.FilterNoneHint: A slot without a reference accepts NOTHING: set template(s), tag or key to open it.
Slot.NoFilter: This slot has no reference set: it accepts nothing (set its filter in the workshop).
Slot.SizeHint: The slot is always square (one dimension, so item icons are not distorted). Empty = 64 px.
Slot.ListKeyHint: Only accepts items whose world item is in this reference list of the item (e.g. the weapon's compatible ammo). Empty list = nothing gets in.
Slot.ListEmpty: No compatible item defined: the list is empty.
Slot.NotListed: This item is not in the list of compatible items.
Slot.EmptyTextHint: Optional. The prompt shown in the empty slot, on the sheet as in the workshop (e.g. "Drop a class"). It uses the value's font and color (Style tab).
Slot.CompatHint: Optional. Pick a dropdown of this template (category, class…). The dropped item declares its compatibilities with checkboxes whose label matches a choice of that dropdown (“Handgun”, “SMG”…): it is accepted only if the checkbox of the current choice is checked. No checkbox checked = fits everywhere.
Slot.Incompatible: This item is not compatible with this one.
Slot.Hidden: This container is not available on this item.
Slot.ShowName: Show the name next to the icon
Slot.ShowNameHint: For a slot read like a label (a class, a job…). The chosen size becomes the icon's size.

Actor.NoTemplatesHint: No character template yet — create a Template first, it will serve all your sheets.
Actor.NeedsTemplate: Cannot create a character without a template: create a Template first.
Actor.DeleteBlocked: Deletion blocked: template “{name}” is used by {count} character(s). Delete those sheets first.
Actor.PJBadgeHint: Automatic: the sheet is owned by a player = PC, otherwise NPC (sheet permissions).
Actor.ThemeUseGlobal: Use the general theme on this template

Native.BadgeHint: Native Foundry component: always present, no key — it points directly to the character.
Native.DialogHint: Native Foundry component — no key or label: it is bound directly to the document (portrait/icon or name), lives in the header and cannot be deleted.
Native.ImgHint: The portrait is also the character's icon. On the sheet, click it to change the image.
Native.CantDelete: This component is native: it is part of every character sheet and cannot be deleted.
Native.ReturnedHeader: Native component returned to the sheet header.
Native.DragHint: Drag into the page: place this native component wherever you want (column, frame…). The trash sends it back to the header.
Native.SubLabelHint: Small text displayed BELOW the name field (e.g. “Identity”, “Subject”). Empty = nothing.

TplTheme.Title: Template theme
TplTheme.UseGlobalHint: Unchecked: this template and all its sheets start from Foundry's native look, then apply the settings below — independent from the rest of the windows.
TplTheme.TitlebarHint: Frame hidden: the title bar takes no space — the sheet and its decorations reach the top; the title (unless hidden) and buttons float above, and the window stays draggable from the top.
TplTheme.ResetContent: Clear all theme settings of this template and return to the general theme?
TplTheme.CustomCssHint: Free CSS, for advanced users. Write “@modele” as a selector: it is automatically replaced by THIS template's windows (e.g.: @modele .window-content { … }).

Deco.Title: SVG decorations
Deco.Hint: Place ornaments on the sheet: an SVG (file or pasted code), anchored wherever you want. A negative offset lets it overhang the window (clip, seal, screws…).
Deco.OffsetHint: From the anchor point. Negative = outward: Y at -30 on top center overhangs above the window.
Deco.SizeHint: Decoration box; the SVG fits inside while keeping its proportions.

TplTheme.SheetSizeHint: Width × height of this template's sheets when opened. Empty = automatic. The window stays resizable — nothing is locked.
TplTheme.HideTitleHint: The title (and its icon) disappears from the bar of this template's sheets and its workshop; the buttons stay. Independent of the theme.
TplTheme.ImportBad: This file is not an SBE template theme.
TplTheme.ImportDone: Theme imported: check it, then save.
TplTheme.ItemIoHint: Same file as a character template theme: an item template only takes the title and sounds from it.
TplTheme.ModeHint: A sheet with its own look (paper, screen…) can keep the same appearance whatever Foundry's mode: fields, texts and colors always use the palette chosen here.

Tooltip.MenuHint: Look of component tooltips: background, frame, font, SVG, advanced CSS.
Tooltip.Title: SBE — Tooltips
Tooltip.Intro: Styles the tooltips configured on components (pencil → Tooltip tab). Everything applies LIVE: hover a component on an open sheet to judge. Foundry's native tooltips are untouched.
Tooltip.TextHint: A color set on a component (Tooltip tab) stays in charge.
Tooltip.BgCodeHint: Takes priority over the path. Automatically sanitized (never executable code).
Tooltip.CssHint: 📍 "@tooltip" (or "@bulle") = the SBE tooltip. E.g.: @tooltip { backdrop-filter: blur(3px); } — also targets .sbe-tt, .sbe-tt-formula, .sbe-tt-src.
Tooltip.ImportBad: This file is not an SBE tooltip export.
Tooltip.ImportDone: Settings imported: check the preview, then click Save.
Tooltip.ThemeColorsHint: Empty color = the theme's (menu background, text, border): the bubble follows the chosen theme.
Tooltip.FollowThemeHint: Foundry always shows its tooltips in dark colors. Checked: they follow each player's interface theme (dark or light).

Roll.OnHint: The field becomes clickable: its label rolls the dice. No extra button — the field keeps its input.
Roll.IdsHint: Optional, comma separated. Free labels shared by several rolls (e.g. physical, talent, attack). For each label, the template key “jet_label”, when it exists, is added to the roll and listed by name in the message. One field then modifies a whole family of rolls. Letters, digits and _ only.
Roll.IdsBad: Invalid roll identifier: letters, digits and _ only, no spaces.
Roll.FormulaHint: Foundry dice expression; the template's KEYS are accepted: 1d100, 1d20 + str_mod, 2d6 + handgun_skill…
Roll.Label: Message title
Roll.CompareTarget: Success if roll ≤ a target value
Roll.CompareHint: "Target value" uses the field below (a number or a key) instead of the field's value. For an attack "1d100 + score against a difficulty", pick "≥ a target value" and tick the difficulty in the roll window.
Roll.ApplyHint: The 2-in-1: the field shows its value AND changes it on click (e.g. HP with "1d6" subtracted = damage). Min/max bounds respected; no effect on a computed field.
Roll.CritSHint: None: no critical success. Fixed value: a number (e.g. 5). Formula: an expression over the sheet's keys, recomputed on every roll — e.g. ceil(luck / 10) + crit_bonus. The direction follows the comparison: “under” → critical when the roll is ≤ the threshold, “over” → when it is ≥. “Condition” mode: a true / false formula that decides on its own — it reads margin (by how much the roll beats the threshold), goal (the threshold), natural (the dice without bonus), rollTotal, diceCount (number of dice), countFace(1) (how many 1s; countFace(5, 6): from 5 to 6) and hasDouble(). Example: margin >= 10.
Roll.CritFHint: Same idea, at the other end of the die: “under” → critical failure when the roll is ≥ the threshold (e.g. 95), “over” → when it is ≤. A critical never fires on the wrong side: no critical success on a failed roll, no critical failure on a successful one. “Condition” mode: e.g. margin <= -10, or countFace(1) >= diceCount / 2 (half the dice show 1).
Roll.CritNeedValue: Critical threshold: enter a value or a formula, or choose “None”.
Roll.CritNeedNumber: Critical threshold as a fixed value: a number is expected.
Roll.NeedFormula: The roll is enabled: please provide a formula (e.g. 1d100).
Roll.NoIconHint: The label stays clickable, but without the d20 in front — on the sheet as on charts. Useful when space is tight or a label icon already sits there.
Roll.IconHint: Shown in front of the clickable label, on the sheet as on charts.
Roll.DlgGroupHint: Checked options appear in a window on click, before the roll. Nothing checked: the roll goes straight out.
Roll.OptAdvHint: Several rolls: keep the best (advantage) or the worst (disadvantage). Best follows the roll's direction: for a roll-under, it is the lowest.
Roll.OptModHint: The player types a number (+10, -5). A bonus always helps: on a roll-under, it raises the threshold.
Roll.OptTargetHint: The roll's target can be changed before rolling. Only used when a comparison is set.
Roll.OptModeHint: Adds the visibility list to the window (the allowed ones below).
Roll.CompareTargetOver: Success if roll ≥ a target value
Roll.CritDie: Criticals read on the die alone
Roll.CritDieHint: Critical thresholds compare the natural dice result, without added bonuses ("1d100 + score": only the d100 counts). A critical then decides the result: critical success = success, critical failure = failure.
Roll.ModeBlind: Blind (only the GM sees the result)
Roll.VisGroupHint: Who reads this roll's message. The roll window ("Message visibility" box above) only offers the allowed visibilities; a single allowed one = forced, no list.
Roll.VisAllowedHint: None checked = all. The default visibility is always allowed.
Roll.NatShift: The natural die shifts one step
Roll.NatShiftHint: Optional, with a comparison. The NATURAL result of the dice (no bonus) raises the result one degree (failure → success → critical success) or lowers it (success → failure → critical failure). Example: 20 and 1 on a d20. Empty = no shift.
Roll.DlgAdvPreset: Preselected (effect or carried item), can be changed.
Roll.SettingAdvLockHint: An imposed advantage or disadvantage (effect, checkbox of a carried item such as a skill) is locked in the roll window. Unchecked: it is only preselected there and the player can change it. Without a window, it always applies.

Lookup.On: Make this table queryable from formulas
Lookup.OnHint: The table becomes consultable: look a value up in a range and read back another column. Useful for what a formula cannot express — armor tiers, injury tables, die ladders. Tip: tick “Hidden on sheet” to keep the table usable without displaying it.
Lookup.RangeHint: The search compares the value against these two columns. Empty high range: the row only matches the exact low value. Outside every range, the nearest row answers.
Lookup.CsvHint: A CSV is a plain-text table that Excel, LibreOffice and Google Sheets all open and save. Prepare your table in a spreadsheet, import it here. Importing REPLACES the existing columns and rows; it applies when you confirm.
Lookup.CsvOk: CSV read: {cols} column(s), {rows} row(s). Confirm to apply.
Lookup.CsvEmpty: Empty or unreadable CSV file (a header row and at least one data row are expected).
Lookup.FormulaHint: table("key"; value; "column") — tableX("key"; value; "searchColumn"; "returnColumn") — tableList("key"; "column") — carried("key"[; "container"]) — carriedCount(["container"])

Free.OnHint: The frame stops stacking its children: in the workshop, grab a component and drop it where you want — any component: text, number, checkbox, slot, image. Nothing can leave the frame: it stretches by itself to contain whatever you place. Horizontal positions are kept as percentages, so the layout holds when the sheet changes width. The ⠿ handle keeps its role: moving the component out of the frame.
Free.UnitPx: Position in PIXELS: anchored to the frame corner — does not move when the window stretches (ideal over an image). Click to switch to %.
Free.UnitPct: Position as a PERCENTAGE: follows the frame width when the window stretches. Click to switch to pixels.

Inv.DisplayHint: The list shows one row per item, with the columns of your choice. The grid shows one cell per item (or stack). The spatial grid gives each item a rectangle of several cells (its size is set on the world item, Media tab).
Inv.GridColsHint: Cells per row. Empty = auto: as many as the sheet width allows.
Inv.GridRowsHint: Empty = infinite: a free row is added as soon as the grid is full. With a number, the grid has columns × rows cells and refuses new items when full (a column count is then required).
Inv.CellSizeHint: Cells are square; the item icon fills them. Empty = 56 px.
Inv.GridSortHint: each item stays in the cell where it is dropped; dropped on a taken cell, it swaps places.
Inv.GridName: Show the name under the icon
Inv.GridNameHint: Otherwise the name shows in the tooltip on hover.
Inv.GridFull: The grid is full: no free cell left.
Inv.AcceptStacksHint: Unchecked: one unit at a time, never asking anything.
Inv.AcceptStacksSlotHint: Unchecked: the slot only takes one unit, even from a stack.
Inv.QtyMaxHint: Total held, all stacks together. Empty = unlimited.
Inv.QtyMaxSlotHint: Total accepted in this slot (a magazine, a hand…). Empty = unlimited.
Inv.ColsHint: One column per item key. The item name always takes the first column.
Inv.ColLabelPh: label (taken from the template if empty)
Inv.FilterShared: The acceptance filter is the same as for slots: what the container takes, or refuses.
Inv.FilterNoneHint: A container with no filter accepts EVERYTHING: it is the bag. Restrict it if needed.
Inv.RemoveConfirm: Delete “{name}” from this sheet? The item is permanently deleted.
Inv.NoContainer: No container can take it: the item stays carried, unstored.
Inv.NoCarrier: This item is carried by nobody: nothing can be stored in it.
Inv.SelfHost: An item cannot be stored inside itself.
Inv.SlotBusy: This slot is already filled with “{name}”.
Inv.ReplaceConfirm: Replace “{old}” with “{neu}”? The outgoing item goes back to the inventory.
Inv.QtyHint: Native component: the stack quantity. Its key is fixed (“quantity”) and there can only be one per template.
Inv.QtyNeedsStack: The template is no longer stackable: this component stays hidden until the option is checked again.
Inv.AskReplaceHint: Unchecked: a filled slot refuses the drop. Checked: the question is asked, and the outgoing item goes back to the inventory.
Inv.IconSizeHint: Size of item icons in the list. Empty = default size.
Inv.NoGroupHint: By default several copies of the same world item share one collapsible row, each keeping its own values. Checked: one row per item.
Inv.CatModeHint: By a key: sections build themselves from the values found on the items. By hand: you write your sections and their filter.
Inv.CatKeyHint: The value of this key on each item becomes a section. If the key is a dropdown, sections follow the order of its choices.
Inv.SubKeyHint: Optional: a second key splitting each section. Empty = no sub-sections.
Inv.CatIconsHint: Optional: an icon in front of the section whose value matches.
Inv.CatsHint: Order matters: an item falls into the first category that accepts it, and a row ticked “sub-cat.” nests under the section written above it.
Inv.CatSubHint: Nest this category under the previous one.
Inv.ModeHint: Reference list: drop WORLD items here (compatible ammo, required tools…). Nothing is carried or moved; a carried copy dropped here is replaced by its world item. The filter below still applies.
Inv.RefNotCarried: A reference list does not hold carried items.
Inv.RefNeedWorld: Drop a world item (or a copy whose world item still exists).
Inv.RefEmpty: Empty list — drop world items here.
Inv.MirrorHint: Optional. This list shows the content of another reference list of the template, read-only (nothing to fill twice). Example: the list filled in Details, shown under the description.
Inv.ReverseHint: Optional. The list shows, read-only, the world items that list THIS item in their list with this key (e.g. on a recipe: the tools whose "recipes" list contains it).
Inv.OwnedOnlyHint: A player only sees the list items their character carries a copy of; if none, the list does not appear. The GM sees everything.
Inv.Unique: Only one copy of each item on the sheet
Inv.UniqueHint: An item the sheet already carries a copy of (same world item) is refused, wherever it is stored.
Inv.EquipsHint: Like a slot: "while equipped" effects, "equipped" lights, equip / unequip triggers and the HUD buttons of equipped items also apply to the items in this container. Example: the attacks and gear grid of a creature.
Inv.ToChat: Send with the description to chat
Inv.ToChatHint: When the item is shown in chat (right click → Show in chat), this list follows the description.
Inv.SpatialHint: Each item takes its size in cells (1 × 1 by default, set on the world item). A single grid, no categories; a stack takes its size only once.
Inv.SpatialSizeHint: Columns × rows: the size of the grid. Both are required.
Inv.SpatialNoRoom: Not enough room in the grid for {name}.
Inv.SpatialBlocked: The item does not fit there.
Inv.SpatialOutHint: These items have no room. Drag them into the grid when there is space.
Inv.SpatialItemHint: The room this item takes in spatial grids (inventories and chests). All its copies follow.
Inv.SpatialItemImgHint: An image drawn for the item's size (for example 1 × 3 for a sword). Empty: the item's icon.
Inv.AfterDrop: After the drop, offer the button
Inv.AfterDropPh: key of a button of the dropped item
Inv.AfterDropHint: Empty: nothing is offered. Otherwise, right after the drop, this button of the dropped item is offered ("Reload" a weapon placed in a trap). In an inventory it acts like a click on the button; in a world item, you choose what is stored with the dropped item, and how many.
Inv.WorldFromScene: Pick up the item placed on the scene first.
Inv.WaitOpenHint: Open the window of waiting items (drop on the ground, throw away, give back).
Inv.WaitHint: These items have no room in this container. Make room, then drag them in.
Inv.Locked: "{name}" is bound to an effect: it cannot be parted with while the effect lasts.
Inv.DisplayCards: Cards (carried items: name, chips, buttons, folding text)
Inv.CardsHint: One card per item: icon and name, chips and boxes (the columns below), a band with the gauge as dots and the item's buttons (those offered outside its sheet), folding text behind the arrow. Sections (sorting) are shown as titles.
Inv.CardLockHint: Formula read on the item. True: the card is greyed, a lock before the name, its buttons disabled.
Inv.CardDescHint: Formula read on the item that gives the text (one of the item's rich texts). Empty, or no result: the item's description. Nothing at all: no arrow.
Inv.CardGaugeHint: Shown as dots in the band (full / empty), with “2/3”. At zero, the card fades.
Inv.CardEmpty: Text when a section is empty
Inv.CardSplitHint: The sorting sections in columns (two sections: two columns).
Inv.CardColsHint: In cards, each column chooses where it goes: chip (under the name), box (right, label above) or tag (under the box). Text: {{key}} and {{= formula}} read on the item (empty = the value). Only if: formula. An empty, 0 or false chip is not shown.
Inv.NotYours: "{name}" is not yours: you cannot take it.

IO.ExportHint: Downloads this template's structure as JSON (no item values, the structure only).
IO.ImportHint: Applies a JSON file's structure to this template: components already present (same key) are updated, new ones added.
IO.NotATemplate: This file is not an SBE template structure.
IO.TooNew: This file comes from a newer version of the engine.
IO.ForActor: This structure is meant for a character template.
IO.ForItem: This structure is meant for an item template.
IO.Empty: This file contains no usable component.
IO.StackableOn: The “stackable” option was turned on: the Quantity component needs it.
IO.SkipQtyActor: the Quantity component only exists on item templates
IO.SkipQtyDouble: there can only be one Quantity component
IO.SkipKeyTaken: key already used in this template ({key})
IO.ReportIntro: “{name}”: {added} component(s) added, {updated} updated (same key: settings, style and position from the file).
IO.SkipBranch: its contents were skipped along with it
IO.SkipNative: native header component already present (or item template)
IO.ThemeApplied: The file's theme will replace this template's theme.
IO.NativeUiApplied: The file's portrait and name (header) settings will replace this template's.
IO.Placed: {n} component(s) placed where requested in the sheet.
IO.PlaceMissing: "{name}": requested place not found — added at the bottom of the template.
IO.ModeQuestion: What should be done with this structure?
IO.ReplaceWarn: REPLACE: the template's structure becomes the file's. Sheet values are kept (by key); a key missing from the file is no longer displayed.
IO.ModeUpdateHint: Update: every component of the file already in the template (same key) takes the file's settings, style and position; new ones are added; inside a container the file describes, whatever it no longer holds is removed; the rest of the template is untouched.
IO.ModeReplaceHint: Replace: the template's structure becomes exactly the file's; whatever it doesn't mention is removed. Either way, sheets keep their values, stored by key.
IO.Removed: {n} component(s) missing from the file removed.
IO.KeptOutside: {n} component(s) missing from the file left in place.
IO.Dismantled: {n} container(s) emptied by the file removed.
IO.DirHint: Directly creates a template (item or character) for each .json file exported from the workshop. Several files at once; you can also drag them onto this tab, or onto a folder to store them there.
IO.DirNotTemplate: “{file}” is not a template exported by SBE.

Stack.CfgHint: How copies of this template gather into stacks.
Stack.MaxHint: Empty or 0 = unlimited. A larger intake splits into several stacks: 100 rounds in boxes of 30 give three full boxes and one of ten.
Stack.NotStackable: The “stackable” option is unchecked: this setting only applies once it is.

Media.DeclaredHint: The media NAMES this template asks for. Each item then sets its own sound and animation behind each name: a shotgun and a pistol don't sound alike.
Media.TabHint: This item's sounds and animations. Only the GM sees this tab.
Media.NoSound: No sound is set on this line.
Media.FalloffHint: Volume decreases with distance, down to silence at the edge of the range.
Media.NameBad: Invalid media name “{name}”: start with a lowercase letter, then only lowercase letters, digits or _ (e.g. shot, part_attached).
Media.LoadFailed: Cannot read "{file}". The file is missing, or its encoding can't be read by the browser (some compressed WAV files, for example). Re-export it as 16-bit PCM WAV, OGG or MP3.
Media.VolumeZero: This sound's volume is set to 0%.
Media.InterfaceMuted: The sound is playing, but your "Interface" slider in Foundry's audio settings is at zero.
Media.NameTaken: The media name “{name}” is already used in this template.
Media.AnimHint: An image or a video (webm, mp4…) played on the scene. Same audience and range as the sound.
Media.AnimScreenHint: For effect videos on a black background: black becomes transparent.
Media.AnimRandomHint: Each play turns the animation randomly: repeated impacts don't look alike.
Media.AnimPlaceHint: Without a target, the animation plays where you aimed (the impact point). As a trail, it starts from the carrier and stretches to the target; size then sets its thickness.
Media.AnimTestHint: Animation played at the scene center: select a token (and target one) to see it in place.
Media.FromModel: This copy's sounds and animations are those of its world item: set them there, every copy follows.
Media.NextHint: For a media played first (an attack's shot): the outcome media (hit, miss, critical) starts after this delay. Empty = when this sound ends; 0 = at the same time.

UiSound.Title: Sheet sounds
UiSound.SheetHint: Played only for the person opening or closing the sheet. Other players hear nothing. Everyone sets their volume with the "Interface" slider in Foundry's audio settings. Leave the file empty for no sound.
UiSound.ClickHint: Played when switching to this tab from another one (not when clicking the tab already open). Only the person clicking hears it. Example: a bag rustle for the Inventory tab.

Identity.RevealTitle: Identity hidden from players — click to reveal
Identity.HideTitle: Identity revealed to players — click to hide
Identity.RevealedMsg: "{name}" is now known to the players.
Identity.HiddenMsg: "{name}" is unknown to the players again.
Identity.SettingEnabledHint: A character without a player owner shows as "Unknown" to players until the GM reveals it (eye button in its sheet header). Covers token nameplates, the combat tracker (and carousels), sheets, the directory and the chat.

Temp.Label: Temporary points
Temp.OnHint: Adds a "+" box next to the gauge (sub-key key_temp, e.g. hp_temp). They take decreases first: HP 30 + 5 temporary, 8 damage → temporary 0, HP 27. Typing directly in the sheet is never absorbed: the box takes exactly what you type.
Temp.StackHint: "Giving" = writing the sub-key with a step, a roll, an effect or a macro (e.g. hp_temp = 8). Writing 0 removes them.
Temp.Minutes: After this many minutes of game time (0 = never)
Temp.ExpireHint: Tick what you want: the first one reached wins. Rounds count down at the start of the bearer's turn; counters restart whenever they receive more. Nothing ticked and 0 everywhere: they stay until used up.

Steps.EditorHint: Steps run in order. A false condition stops everything and shows its message — and greys out the button (sheet, inventory right-click) with that message on hover.
Steps.RollKeyPh: key of the field to roll

Hint.place: The item leaves the inventory and becomes a scene object (token): aiming with preview, mouse wheel to rotate. Its template must be a "Scene object". Put it last: afterwards the item is no longer in the bag. Or: summon creatures (world NPCs) aimed on the map, or dismiss one's summons.
Hint.condition: Continues only if the formula is true; otherwise shows the message.
Hint.consume: Removes an amount from a field of the item, from items held in a slot (rounds in a magazine), from a field of the character carrying the item (mana, stamina…), or from THIS item itself (the stack goes down and disappears at zero: a drunk potion).
Hint.roll: Rolls the roll set on this field — of the item, or of the carrier. On the carrier, the key is a formula read on the item (talent, picked_talent) or a character key in quotes ("crafting"); a label like "Crafting" is turned into its key. Optional difficulty (+ = harder). Next steps read the result: isSuccess, isCrit, isFumble (1 or 0) and rollTotal; after an attack, isHit.
Hint.set: Changes a field with the formula (dice allowed, e.g. 2d6 + 2): replace it, add to it, subtract from it, or give temporary points (gauge that accepts them). Add and subtract stay within the field's bounds. On the item, the character carrying it, the targets (last attack or "Choose a target", otherwise marked tokens) or the chosen item. The GM writes for you if you do not own the target.
Hint.fill: Reloads the slot from the carrier's inventory: a window offers the ammo (if several compatible kinds) and the amount, maximum by default.
Hint.empty: Returns the whole content of the slot to the carrier's inventory.
Hint.effect: Applies, removes or changes the stacks of an effect, on the item's carrier or on targeted tokens (the GM applies it if you don't own the target).
Hint.attack: Picks the target (marked with T, otherwise click a token), checks range, rolls the target's defense then this field's roll against it (tie = hit), and computes damage reduced according to the Combat manager. Cancelling the target choice stops the button: place "Consume" AFTER this step. Afterwards, the following steps read its result (isSuccess, isCrit, isFumble, rollTotal), and "on the targets" aims at the targets hit.
Hint.target: The player aims at a character: tokens marked with T, otherwise a click on a token (themselves included). Following "on the targets" steps aim at it. Optional range in squares. "Who can be targeted": everyone, allies, enemies… (by token disposition); "Only if": a formula read on the target's sheet (hp <= 0: a fallen ally) — refused, the button stops with the message.
Hint.pick: A window offers items passing the filter (formula read on each item; fields of the item in use have the self_ prefix): those carried by the character, or those of a reference list of this item (a tool's recipes). Optional display text next to each name. The chosen item can then be read: pickedName, and its fields prefixed picked_ (picked_ing1…).
Hint.sound: Plays a media declared by the template (item's Media tab): sound, animation, or both. The animation aims at the target of the last attack or of "Choose a target" (otherwise the targeted tokens), or the aimed point. Several "Play a media" in a row chain: each waits the "Next media after" delay of the previous one. After an attack, "Only if" can read isHit (a target was hit), isSuccess, isCrit, isFumble and rollTotal.
Hint.wait: The following steps happen when the time is up: rounds in combat, minutes out of combat (one replaces the other when empty). Choosing a target, an item or a roll goes BEFORE this step. A card with "Cancel" is shown.
Hint.land: For a recoverable projectile (throwing knife, arrow…): after the attack, one unit leaves the stack and goes, depending on whether the attack HIT or MISSED, into the target's inventory, on the ground (where it fell, picked up by a nearby token) or is destroyed. Text or formula: "target", "ground" or "destroyed" (an item list key works too).
Hint.quest: Acts on a quest of a quest journal: give it (announced to its section), advance an objective (checkbox checked, or counter + the number, which can be a formula), reveal or hide an objective, or change the status (completed / failed / cancelled distribute like the journal's buttons). Run by a player, the GM executes it.
Hint.take: Removes items from the carrier's inventory: copies of a world item, those passing a filter (candidate's keys; "self_key" for the item in use), or the item named by a formula (its name, e.g. picked_ing1; empty = nothing to take). If there are not enough, nothing is removed and the button stops (custom message). "Check only" verifies without removing: put these checks BEFORE the removals.
Hint.give: Gives items to the carrier: a world item, or the one a formula names (its name or id; a table or a roll can choose it). Stored in the inventory, outside the grid without room, or at their feet without a container. Crafting result, loot…
Hint.scene: Acts on the scene elements LINKED to the placed item (GM: panel footer → Scene links). The group is the label given to links; empty, all links of the right type. Teleport: the acting character goes to the first link of the group. Trap: acts on the trap itself (disarm, take it, take its contents and destroy the trap, re-arm, camouflage again, reveal it to the acting character, hide it from everyone again). Open a placed item's panel: opens the panel of the first link that has one (a placed item, or the item attached to the linked tile, door or region), even far away: a terminal opens the distant door; its buttons work while it stays open.
Hint.useslot: Runs a button of the item held in one of this item's slots (Fire, Reload, Unload…), by the same character and on the same targets. Greyed out if the slot is empty or that button is impossible.
Hint.ask: A window asks one or more questions; each answer takes the name given to the question and can be read by the next steps (formulas, conditions, "Only if": "burst", "aim_head"…). Who answers: the acting character, the GM, or the player of the first target. Cancel stops the button without doing anything. After a wait, the default values are used.
Hint.signal: Sends a signal (a free name) to the acting character, the targets, or everyone in the scene (characters and placed items): their buttons set to "Runs by itself → Signal received" with this name fire. Alarm, chain reaction, trap wired to a door…
Hint.if: Block: if the condition is true, runs the “Then” steps; otherwise the “Else” steps. A branch may stay empty. A block may hold another one (two levels at most).
Hint.result: Block: runs the branch matching the LAST roll or attack of this button (critical success, success, failure, critical failure). With no roll before it, no branch runs.
Hint.table: Draws from a Foundry random table. The result becomes a variable for the next steps: tableResult (the drawn text) and tableTotal (the rolled number) — an “If…” block can use it (tableResult == "Severe wound"). Checked, a drawn item (world item) is given to the carrier.
Hint.time: Moves the calendar's time: advance or rewind by a duration (a formula, dice included), go to the next part of the day or back to the previous one, or set an hour, a date. "Keep the current weather": the weather from before stays imposed until the next change; otherwise it is the one of the new moment. Done by the GM (a player sends it to them).
Hint.weather: Decided: imposes a weather type (by its key) for a duration, or with no end if the duration is empty. Natural: removes the imposed weather, the normal draw resumes.
Hint.season: Decided: imposes a season (by its key) for a duration, or with no end if the duration is empty — an "eternal winter". Temperatures, sun and drawn weather follow that season. Natural: the season follows the date again.
Hint.moon: Decided: imposes a phase on a moon (by its key) for a duration, or with no end if the duration is empty — a blood moon raised by a spell. Its effects, display, moon() formulas and the "phase change" trigger follow. Natural: the moon goes back to its cycle.
Hint.resist: Makes the resistance roll of an effect applied to the character, as the effect sets it (field, difficulty; success: cancelled or reduced, critical failure: worsened), with advantage or disadvantage if chosen. Empty key: the effect that launched the button ("Runs by itself → Effect applied"); this roll then replaces the one the effect makes when applied. "Depending on the roll result" can follow.
Hint.level: Gives (or takes away, with a negative number) experience or levels of a Level component, named by its key: to the button's document, to the targets, or to carried items of a chosen template. Experience is added to the component's XP key; levels are available to take or applied right away.

Atk.DefensePh: roll on the target's sheet (e.g. 1d100 + dodge)
Atk.ZoneHint: Empty: single-target attack. Otherwise a zone name: circle, cone, line, or a template drawn in "Area templates". Text or formula (e.g. the zone type of the loaded ammo).
Atk.SavePh: roll field on the target's sheet
Atk.ProfileHint: The profile (Combat manager) gives the defense, damage type, zone, save and roll-window options. On the weapon: the roll (field above), damage, range and, if needed, the number of hits.
Atk.AdvancedHint: A field filled here replaces the profile's, for this weapon only. Empty = as the profile.
Atk.UnblockHint: Unblockable: the target(s) make no roll (no defense, dodge, parry or area save); the attacker still rolls. "Ask" opens a small window before aiming. "Ignore defense if…" is read on the target's sheet.
Atk.PushHint: The hit target is pushed N squares: along the shooter's axis for one target, from the center for an area (× the area share). A wall stops the push.
Atk.PushSavePh: none, half or full (or a key)
Atk.MediaHint: The shot media plays first (sound, and animation as a trail toward the target or the missed point). Then the outcome one — critical (otherwise the hit one), hit, miss — right after: when the shot sound ends, or after the delay set on the shot line in the item's Media tab. Burst: the shot and its outcome replay as many times as the repeats (empty = the step's number of hits), spaced by the interval. Names declared by the template.
Atk.SaveHint: Each target hit by the area defends itself: either with a roll field of ITS sheet (“Target save”), or with ITS DEFENSE (the defense formula of the attack or profile) against the attack roll total — a tie is a dodge. Success: half damage, or none (“Successful save”: a word or a key of the weapon). Unblockable or defenseless target: no roll.
Atk.SaveModePh: half or none (or a key of the weapon)
Atk.SaveVsDefense: its defense against the attack roll
Atk.LocHint: Where the hit zone on the target's body comes from (Combat manager → Bodies and zones). Read from the attack roll: the formula knows natural (dice alone) and rollTotal, e.g. reverse(natural) or natural % 10. Empty = a draw over the body's ranges.
Atk.NonLethalHint: If the condition is true (often a roll-window checkbox: non_lethal), the target's damage key does not drop below the kept value. A target that reaches it receives the chosen effect. The card shows "Non-lethal".

Steps.NoCarrier: This item is not carried by any character.
Steps.LoadPickHint: Several compatible ammo types: pick which to load. One other than the current replaces it (the old one goes back to the bag).
Steps.PickFilterPh: filter on the item (e.g. durability < durability_max)
Steps.NoPicked: No item chosen: place "Choose an item" before.
Steps.InteractiveAfterWait: "{step}" cannot come after "Wait": nobody is there to choose at the end. Place it before.
Steps.PickShowPh: text shown next to the name (e.g. condition)
Steps.LandHitPh: target, ground or destroyed (or a key)
Steps.PickFromList: a reference list of the item

NewDay.Title: New day
NewDay.CommonHint: Applied to all checked characters. Key of a number or gauge field of your templates + signed amount (number or formula), as a value or as a % of the field's maximum. E.g. hunger → -2 value. The result stays within the field's bounds.
NewDay.TiersHint: A tier is chosen for each character. Amount as a value or as a % of the field's maximum. E.g. "Decent night": hp → 25 % of max.
NewDay.NightHint: Advances game time by as much: effect durations and everything that follows time run on their own. 0: time does not move. Can be changed for each night in the Rest tab.
NewDay.NoActors: No character owned by a player.
NewDay.ModeHint: By tiers: each character gets the chosen tier (good night, bad night…). Over time: each line gives its amount every N minutes, multiplied by each character's rest duration. Common changes apply in both modes.
NewDay.RateHint: Each line gives back its amount every N minutes, as many times as the rest duration allows. E.g. hp → 10 % of max every 30 minutes: 8 h of rest = 16 times. It stops at the maximum.
NewDay.RestDefaultHint: Offered to each character, can be changed on their line in the Rest tab.
NewDay.ActorsHintTime: Check those who rest and set each one's duration (one sleeps 8 h, another keeps watch 4 h). Game time advances by the longest rest.
NewDay.ActorsHintTiers: Check those who rest and choose each one's tier (decent night, bad night…).

Effects.Title: Effects
Effects.MenuHint: Define your effects (conditions, buffs, penalties): what they modify on your sheets, their duration, their stacks.
Effects.PickOrCreate: Pick an effect from the list, or create one.
Effects.Label: Name
Effects.KeyHint: Unique identifier: a lowercase letter first, then lowercase letters, digits and _ — the rule of every SBE key. It must not reuse a native Foundry condition's id.
Effects.ChangesHint: One line per key of your character templates (number, or gauge bounds "key_max" / "key_min"). Amount: number or formula read on the sheet. Nothing is written into values: the sheet shows the total, colored, with the breakdown on hover. Applied order: multiply, add, at most, at least, override.
Effects.DurationHint: In combat, the effect loses one round at each new round; outside combat, it follows game time. 0 = no limit for that counter. At zero, the effect is removed.
Effects.StackHint: Stackable: in the token HUD, left click +1, right click −1 (removed at 0).
Effects.GroupHint: Optional. Two effects of the same group cannot coexist: applying one removes the other (e.g. fatigue levels).
Effects.NoDefenseHint: The bearer no longer rolls defense, dodge, parry or area saves when attacked (stunned, paralyzed, asleep…).
Effects.DeleteActive: It is applied on {n} character(s) — these effects will be removed:
Effects.ImportDone: {n} effect(s) added, {r} updated, {s} skipped (invalid key or name of a core condition). Saved.
Effects.KeyBad: the key must start with a lowercase letter, then only lowercase letters, digits or _.
Effects.KeyNative: this key is a Foundry native condition id.
Effects.ResistNoRoll: Resistance roll: field "{key}" has no roll configured.

Trigger.Title: Trigger
Trigger.Hint: The effect applies itself when the conditions become true, and goes away when they fail. A triggered effect does not prevent applying it by hand.
Trigger.ConditionsHint: Formulas on the sheet: your keys, maxOf("key"), minOf("key"), hasEffect("key"), stacksOf("key"), inCombat(). E.g. hp <= maxOf("hp") * 0.25
Trigger.EventsHint: Apply the effect when they happen; it then follows its duration (no automatic removal).

Periodic.Title: Periodic effect
Periodic.Hint: Changes a key every turn, round or game-time interval (damage or healing over time). The result stays within the field's bounds; the amount follows stacks if that option is checked.
Periodic.ReduceHint: A loss is reduced by this key's value (your resistance to the damage type), never turning into a gain.

Zero.qty: Remove 1 from the stack (the next starts full)

Periodic.TargetHint: "The item granting the effect": the key changes on the item (its battery, its charges…), and only while the effect lasts — nothing wears out while the item is off or stowed. With "Nothing", add "key > 0" to the item rule's "Only if": the effect drops by itself at zero.

Resist.Title: Resistance roll
Resist.Hint: Uses the roll already configured on a sheet field (pencil → Dice roll), made harder by the difficulty. Success: the effect goes away, or loses stacks (rounds if not stackable).
Resist.Crit: Criticals: reduction multiplied on a critical success, worsening on a critical failure

Esc.Title: Escalation and tiers
Esc.Hint: Stacks rise on their own at the chosen cadence, up to the maximum. With "decay", they go down when the trigger no longer holds (the effect goes away at zero).
Esc.Decay: Decay when the trigger no longer holds
Esc.TiersHint: Optional. Each tier replaces the effect's name, icon and changes at that level; the number of tiers becomes the maximum.
Esc.RiseHint: "Only when added": tiers exist but nothing rises on its own — the zone (+1 stack each turn inside), an item button or the HUD makes it rise. Cadence and decay are then unused.
Esc.Rise_auto: On their own, at the chosen cadence

Rest.Title: Rest recovery
Rest.Hint: On the new day, for each character going through it.

Effects.NativesHint: All Foundry conditions: click to edit them like an SBE effect (name, icon, changes, duration, trigger…). The eye hides them from the HUD, the arrow restores the original.
Effects.NativeEditHint: Native condition: its key is Foundry's and cannot change.
Effects.KeyNotNative: this key is not a native condition id.

Phases.Title: Phases (chaining)
Phases.Hint: To chain several stages (e.g. a bonus, then a crash). Adding a phase switches everything to phases: the duration and changes above become phase 1.
Phases.Label: Phase name
Phases.HintOn: The effect follows its phases in order: when a phase's duration runs out it moves to the next one; after the last one, it ends. A phase without duration lasts until removed. Deleting all phases 2, 3… turns it back into a simple effect.
Phases.Start: Start of the effect (effect's name and icon)

Look.Title: Look and sound
Look.SoundHint: Played when applied, or looped while the effect lasts. Same rules as item media: who hears, range in scene units, falloff.
Look.TokenHint: Token tint (display only), big icon in the center, and discreet effect: the icon is only seen by the GM and the owner. Stacked effects show ×N on the token.
Look.LightHint: Written on the token while the effect lasts; the original light comes back afterwards. If several effects emit light, the strongest wins.
Look.PersonalHint: The light is not set on the token: only the one looking through it sees it (goggle glow, an animation over the view). Otherwise everyone sees it. "@key": a box on the item decides.
Look.ValueHint: Each field: a number, a formula read on the bearer's sheet, or "@key" read on the item granting the effect — one effect then serves every item of a template, each with its own settings.
Look.AnimHint: An image or a video that loops on the token while the effect lasts (aura, fog…). A discreet effect only shows it to the GM and the owner.
Look.SightHint: While the effect lasts, the bearer sees with this mode ("Vision modes" manager). Several modes at once: the mode's priority decides. Range and angle: number, formula (bearer's sheet) or "@key" (item granting the effect); empty = the token's.

Effects.NativesHideAll: Hide all the ones I have not customized
Effects.NativeResetConfirm: Restore "{name}" to its original Foundry state? Your changes to this condition will be lost.
Effects.DupNative: "{name}" already exists: it is the Foundry condition "{native}". Edit it in the Foundry conditions list instead of creating a duplicate.
Effects.DupName: Two effects are named "{name}": rename one of them.
Effects.IconColorHint: The white of the icon takes this color (black and shadows stay), everywhere: token HUD, icons on the token, sheets, tooltips, chat. A colored copy is stored in the world folder (sbe-icons) when saving.
Effects.IconPaintFailed: Colored icon for "{src}" not created ({err}). Check that the GM can upload files.

Vision.Hint: Without this box, the token's base sight (set in Foundry) stays: a lamp only needs its light, which adds up. With it, sight is REPLACED while the item is lit (goggles), then restored as it was. Only one item counts at a time: the last one turned on; a "Blind" effect beats everything.

Effects.FoundryStatusHint: Foundry's core also treats the bearer as having this status (blind: no vision, invisible, prone, flying…); modules that read it recognize it. Foundry's base conditions (Blind, Invisible…) already do this on their own: this setting is for your own effects (smoke, flash…) or to make one condition count as another. An effect already applied takes the setting on its next application.

Gives.Title: Given items
Gives.Hint: While the effect lasts, the character receives these world items (the weapons of a form, the weapon of a spell…). Drag them here from the sidebar.
Gives.WhereHint: Key of a container or slot of the sheet. Full container: the item waits in its waiting area. Occupied slot: the item in place goes back where it came from, then returns to the slot when the effect ends.
Gives.LockHint: While the effect lasts, the player can neither throw it away, give it, nor put it anywhere else.
Gives.WorldOnly: Drag a world item (sidebar or compendium).
Gives.NeedWhere: {name}: each given item must say where it goes (key of a container or slot).
Gives.Missing: Effect "{effect}": a given item no longer exists.
Gives.NoKey: {actor}: no container or slot "{key}" to receive {name}.

Effects.CategoryHint: Optional, free and not exclusive (unlike the exclusive group): several effects of the same category can coexist. Targeted by "Runs by itself → Effect applied" buttons and by the effectCategory("key") formula.

Grants.Title: Granted effects
Grants.Hint: While an item of this template is equipped (placed in a slot of the sheet, or in a container whose items are equipped) or simply carried, its carrier has the effect; it goes away with the item. "@key" reads the effect key on each item (a field of the item). An effect applied by hand is never removed. "Only if": a formula read on the item (e.g. a "lit" box); the effect is granted only while it is true.

Gauge.MaxFormulaHint: Replaces the maximum above with a formula read on the sheet (e.g. carrying capacity: ceil((strength + con) / 4)). The "key_max" sub-key is always added.
Gauge.ComputedHint: The value comes from the formula (e.g. carried weight: carried("weight")): nothing to type, the gauge follows by itself.
Gauge.DisplayHint: A bar, or one icon per point (hunger, fatigue…) — clicking an icon sets the value. Icon: Font Awesome class.
Gauge.BlockMaxHint: Hard cap: any addition (item picked up, traded, crafted, growing stack, item stored…) that would push this gauge above its maximum is refused. Removing is always allowed, even when over.
Gauge.BlockMsgHint: Message shown when an attempt is refused. Empty = default message. Placeholders: {nom} (character), {objet}, {jauge}, {avant}, {apres}, {max}.
Gauge.BlockGmHint: Checked: the GM is refused like a player. Unchecked: the GM sees the overflow and chooses to continue or cancel.
Gauge.OverflowHint: What the gauge cannot take goes into another key of the same sheet instead of being lost. Example: fatigue going below 0 makes the rest come off health. That key then gets its own bounds (and can overflow further).
Gauge.OverLow: What goes below the minimum is taken from (key)
Gauge.OverHigh: What goes above the maximum is added to (key)
Gauge.OverRatioHint: Multiplies what overflows: 1 = all of it, 0.5 = half.
Gauge.OverBadKey: Invalid overflow key: “{key}” (another key of the sheet).

RollReq.NoRollFields: No roll field in your character templates: first enable “Roll on label click” on a field (workshop → pencil → Dice roll).
RollReq.Title: Request a roll
RollReq.DifficultyHint: Optional. −20 makes the roll harder, +20 easier. Shown on the card.
RollReq.NeedTwo: An opposed roll needs at least two participants.
RollReq.NoChar: No character of yours for this roll.
RollReq.NoField: {name} does not have this roll on their sheet.
RollReq.KeyBHint: Optional. When set (Attack vs Dodge), each token is put on Attack or Defense.
RollReq.WinHint: Best success: a success beats a failure, a critical success beats a success, then the biggest margin; if nobody succeeds, nobody wins.
RollReq.NeedPC: Check at least one character, or “All player characters”.
