RollReq.PickToken: Select the token of the character to roll for.
RollReq.NobodyHas: No player character has this roll on their sheet.
RollReq.Skipped: Without this roll on their sheet, removed from the opposed roll: {names}.

ItemPreview.Hidden: This item isn't visible to players.

ItemFx.OwnTitle: Effect manager effects: when to apply
ItemFx.OwnHint: To apply an effect from the effect manager with this item (own effects are set in their panel above). "While": the effect stays while the item is equipped or carried. "Button": as soon as the button is used, depending on its roll. Never overwritten by a template update.
ItemFx.Empty: No rule yet: add one to say when an effect is applied.
ItemFx.LocalSectionHint: Effects that only exist on this item, without cluttering the effect manager. They use the item's name and icon. Each one unfolds: at the top, WHEN it is applied (an item button, while equipped or carried); below, what it does (duration, changes, phases, periodic effect…). Everything is saved as you type. Once on a character, it keeps going even if the item is consumed.
ItemFx.LocalDeleteConfirm: Delete this own effect? Rules using it will show ⚠; an effect already applied to a character keeps going until it ends.
ItemFx.TriggerHint: When this effect is applied. With a button: as soon as it is used, even if the use takes time; its duration starts then.
ItemFx.InheritHint: This copy follows the effects of its world item "{name}": changing them there changes them for every copy, including those already handed out.
ItemFx.InheritFork: Change them for this copy only
ItemFx.TipShow: Show the effects in the item tooltip
ItemFx.TipShowHint: When hovering the carried item: each effect it gives (from the template or its own) and what it does. A discreet effect stays hidden from players.
ItemFx.OnlyIfHint: Formula read on the item: the effect is granted only while it is true (a checked box, a charge left…). Empty: always.

Combat.MenuHint: Key that takes damage, critical, damage types and their reductions.
Combat.DamageKeyHint: The sheet gauge that loses the damage (hit points…). Temporary points and bounds are respected.
Combat.CritMultHint: Damage from a critical success is multiplied by this value (1 = no bonus).
Combat.TypesHint: For each type, the key read on the TARGET's sheet and subtracted from damage (armor, resistance…). The name must match the type given by the weapon; a type missing from the list is not reduced.
Combat.PickTarget: Click the target (Escape or right-click to cancel).
Combat.OutOfRange: Target out of range: {d} squares for a range of {r}.
Combat.ImportBad: This file is not an SBE combat rules export.
Combat.ImportDone: Rules imported: check them, then click Save.
Combat.ImportMissing: {n} key(s) not found in your character templates: {keys}. They are kept (⚠); create them or pick others.
Combat.ZonesHint: Who is hit by a zone. A template can have its own settings ("Area templates" manager).
Combat.CoverHint: Minimum part of a square (or of the token) the zone must cover. 1% = the smallest bit is enough; 100% = fully covered.
Combat.MeasureCells: the squares occupied by the token
Combat.MeasureHint: Square or hex cells, depending on the scene. A gridless scene always measures on the token. A large token is hit if any one of its cells is.
Combat.WallsHint: Checked from the zone's anchor point: what a wall hides does not count as covered.
Combat.GroundOn: Roll to aim at the ground
Combat.GroundHint: A zone placed on the ground (no token aimed) asks for a roll against a DC: base + a part tied to distance (from 0 to the range). Missed — or missed on an aimed token — the zone scatters.
Combat.ScatterHint: The zone lands at a random distance between the minimum and a limit that grows with the shot's distance, in a random direction.
Combat.ProfileMissing: The attack profile "{name}" does not exist (Combat manager).
Combat.UnblockAsk: Can this attack be dodged, parried or avoided?
Combat.ProfilesHint: Set once, picked by weapons ("Attack" step). Changing a rule here changes it for every weapon using the profile.
Combat.MessagesHint: Who reads attack messages. This setting applies to every attack, over the weapon roll's own setting. "Attacker, targets and GM": a whisper to the attacking player, to the owners of the target(s), and to the GM.
Combat.GmDetailsHint: Readers see the attack and its outcome (hit, miss); the numbers (rolls, defense, damage) go in a second message for the GM only.
Combat.SureHit: Always hits: no defense, no roll.
Combat.FixHint: One button per target: undo, half, normal, double, or give the damage back as healing; only the difference is applied. Selected tokens take the same damage, with their own reduction.
Combat.FixNoSel: First select one or more tokens (not already hit).

Marks.Title: Icon markers
Marks.Hint: Markers computed for each item from its own values: ammo, charges, condition… They show wherever a carried item shows its icon (grids, lists, slots, HUD), never on world or compendium items. Formulas: the template's keys, plus carried(), carriedCount(), carriedValue() for what the item holds.
Marks.Empty: No marker yet: add one below.
Marks.DimHint: The icon turns dark grey while the condition is true (empty weapon, broken item…).
Marks.HaloHint: Rules are read in order: the first true one colors the icon. Put the most serious first.
Marks.Imported: Markers imported: check them, then save.
Marks.ImportBad: This file is not an SBE marker export.

Zone.MenuHint: Blast, breath, spray area templates… drawn freely, with their intensity and color.
Zone.PickOrCreate: Pick an area template on the left, or create one.
Zone.Name: Name
Zone.PropsHint: The white dot is the anchor, the arrow shows the area template's front (toward the mouse in play). Measured in squares: the area template keeps its proportions on every map. The color is a code for your players (red = fire, green = gas…); intensity sets the transparency.
Zone.ToolHint_select: Click a piece to pick it (its intensity is shown), drag it to move it. Delete erases it.
Zone.ToolHint_poly: One click per point. Double-click, or click the first point, to close. Escape cancels.
Zone.ToolHint_ellipse: Drag from the center. Shift: circle.
Zone.ToolHint_rect: Drag from one corner to the other.
Zone.NeedName: Each area template needs a name.
Zone.ImportBad: This file is not an SBE area templates export.
Zone.ImportDone: {added} area template(s) added, {replaced} replaced. Click Save to keep them.
Zone.Unknown: The zone "{name}" does not exist (neither circle, cone, line, nor a drawn area template).
Zone.NoScene: A zone attack needs a displayed scene.
Zone.NeedToken: Your character needs a token on the scene.
Zone.AimSelf: Orient the zone with the mouse (wheel: rotate), click to confirm. Escape or right-click: cancel.
Zone.AimImpact: Place the zone (on a token to aim at it), wheel: rotate, click to confirm. Escape or right-click: cancel.
Zone.AimMiss: Aimed token: missed ({total} against {goal}), the zone scatters by {cases} squares.
Zone.GroundMiss: Ground aim missed ({total} against DC {goal}), the zone scatters by {cases} squares.
Zone.Missing_circle: Circle zone without a radius: set a radius (step or profile).
Zone.Missing_cone: Cone without a length: give the weapon a range (or a length).
Zone.Missing_line: Line without a length: give the weapon a range (or a length).

ItemTip.ElOptionHint: When hovering the item (inventory, slot…), this field shows with its label and value, in the template's order. A number at 0 or an unchecked box is not shown.
ItemTip.ChoiceColorsHint: Optional: check a choice to give it a color. It follows the value wherever it shows (tags, item tooltip). E.g. Rare = blue, Broken = red.
ItemTip.HeaderColor: Colored tag at the top of the item tooltip
ItemTip.HeaderColorHint: This list's value shows first in the tooltip, as a tag written in its color (e.g. "RARE" in blue). A choice without a color is not shown. One list per template.
ItemTip.NoDefault: Not in the tooltip when at its default value
ItemTip.NoDefaultHint: For lists and texts that say nothing at their default value ("Area: None"). Numbers at 0 and unchecked boxes are already hidden. A field hidden by "Visible if" (its own or its frame's) does not appear either.
ItemTip.SignedHint: The number reads signed in the tooltip: +10 in green, −10 in red.

AtkOpt.Hint: They show in the window before aiming. Their key works in every formula of the button: checked box = 1, else 0; number = the value; list = the chosen text. E.g. Focus (focus) → Consume "focus ? 3 : 1".
AtkOpt.HintWeapon: Options added to the profile's, for this weapon (same key = the weapon's wins).
AtkOpt.Label: Label
AtkOpt.BadKey: Option "{key}": invalid key (letters, digits, _; no leading digit).
AtkOpt.NoChoices: The option "{key}" is a list with no choices.

Hud.MenuHint: The characters' action bar: one HUD per character template (menus, submenus, slots, lists, look).
Hud.Title: HUD
Hud.PickerHint: Each character template has its own HUD. Choose the template to configure.
Hud.PickerNone: No character template in this world.
Hud.Enabled: Enable the HUD for this template
Hud.EnabledHint: The HUD shows for the controlled character (selected token; for a player without a token: their assigned character).
Hud.DirectRun: Item with a single action: clicking runs it
Hud.SrcHint: Drag a source into the tree (double-click: add at the end of the bar). Drop on the middle of a menu to put it inside.
Hud.SrcModelsHint: Drag an item from the sidebar into the tree: it shows when the character carries a copy.
Hud.TreeEmpty: The HUD is empty: drag sources here from the left column.
Hud.DelMenuWarn: The menu "{name}" holds {n} entry(ies); they will be removed too.
Hud.MoveIntoSelf: A menu cannot be placed inside one of its own submenus.
Hud.DropNotObject: Only an item can be dropped here.
Hud.Label: Label
Hud.ListHint: The list's items show one by one. "Sort by" creates a submenu per value of the item's field (school: Fire, Light…), in the order and colors of the choices.
Hud.ModelHint: Shows the copy of "{name}" carried by the character (nothing if they have none).
Hud.LookColorsHint: Two themes, dark and light, each with its own colors: the HUD uses the same one as Foundry. The defaults are the old HUD's metal grey.
Hud.LookColorsOrder: The color set on an entry (Configuration) tints its edge.
Hud.DecoHint: Ornaments around the bar: an SVG (pasted code or file), anchored where you want. A negative offset overflows.
Hud.ImportBad: This file is not an SBE HUD.
Hud.ImportDone: HUD imported: check it, then save.
Hud.ImportMissing: Keys missing from this template (kept, flagged ⚠): {keys}
Hud.EffectsHint: Left click: apply the effect (or +1 stack). Right click: remove it (or −1 stack).
Hud.EffectsAuto: automatic trigger: the engine may take it back
Hud.EffectsFail: This effect could not be changed.
Hud.ElOptionHint: The value shows under the item in the HUD (ammo, charges…).
Hud.AlphaHint: Each color has its own opacity: below 100%, the bar and menus show the map through, blurred ("Background blur" setting).
Hud.SettingHideHotbarHint: Hides Foundry's macro bar for you only. The HUD button does the same.
Hud.SettingResetPosHint: Puts the HUD back at its starting position, set by the GM (default: centered, at 80% of the screen height).
Hud.ResetPosDone: HUD moved back to its default place.
Hud.ScreenTip: Click or drag to place the HUD on the screen.
Hud.StartPosHint: The CENTER of the HUD is placed at these screen percentages: 50 / 80 = centered, at 80% of the height (default). Each player can then move it; 'Reset position' (system settings) brings it back here.
Hud.BtnWidthHint: Widths: 0 = automatic. HUD width: the whole bar (automatic buttons stretch inside). Button width: each button.
Hud.HeadHint: Portrait and name are ticked separately. Top / bottom: on one line; left / right: in a column, the name written top to bottom. The header is the handle to move the HUD. The small buttons follow the header by default, or go wherever you want.
Hud.MinisHint: As many as you like. "Item action": the key of an item template button (e.g. allumer) — the small button only shows if the character has an EQUIPPED item with that button, and runs it. "Sheet button": a button of this character template. "Pressed if": a formula read on the item (e.g. allume).

AtkPrev.Hint: "Label: text" lines shown in the roll window, recalculated while the player ticks options or changes the modifier. In the text, each formula in braces is replaced by its value: the weapon's keys, carrier("key") for the wielder, option keys, mod (modifier) and adv (1 advantage, −1 disadvantage). Example: {ex}
AtkPrev.HintWeapon: Empty = the profile's lines. Filled here, they replace the profile's for this weapon. Formulas in braces are recalculated with the chosen options.
AtkPrev.Label: Label

Use.Busy: A use is already in progress.
Use.PendingIntro: {n} item use(s) are still "in progress" (Wait step not finished). Out of combat, they wait for world time to advance.
Use.PendingHint: Cancelling only removes the wait: nothing is refunded or applied. Removing an item's effect (cross on the Effects component) also cancels its wait.

Ground.NotDroppable: "{name}" can't be put on the ground.
Ground.SettingDistance: Picking up an item on the ground: distance (squares)
Ground.SettingDistanceHint: Maximum distance (in squares) between the selected token and a ground item to open it, and to drop an item by drag and drop. 0 = no limit. The GM is never limited.
Ground.Gone: This item is no longer there.
Ground.SelectToken: Select your token to pick up the item.
Ground.NoToken: The carrier has no token on the scene.
Ground.SettingBagHint: Token image when several items lie at the same spot (a bag, like a small temporary chest).
Ground.NoRecipient: No other player character to give to.
Ground.SettingSizeHint: Token size of an item or bag lying on the ground, in cells (0.6 = a bit more than half a cell).
Ground.DeployAsk: {name} can be installed on the scene. Install it here, or drop it on the ground?

PZone.Title: Persistent zone
PZone.TabHint: A zone that stays on the scene after the item is used: a burning fire, smoke, a gas cloud, a healing aura. It only gives or removes effects from the manager: damage, healing and penalties are set in the effect.
PZone.Inherit: This copy follows its template "{name}": its zone is set on the template.
PZone.InheritOn: Zone set on the world item (nature: {nature}).
PZone.InheritOff: The world item leaves no zone.
PZone.NatureHint: The word shared by zones of the same kind: fire, water, smoke… A lowercase letter first, then lowercase letters, digits or _. Natures already in use are suggested.
PZone.NatureMissing: Without a nature, the zone will not apply.
PZone.NatureBad: Badly formed nature: a lowercase letter first, then lowercase letters, digits or _ (no accent or space). The zone will not apply.
PZone.ShapeHint: A cone or a line starts from the caster, turned toward the aimed point. An attached zone follows the token as it moves.
PZone.DurationHint: Two clocks start when the zone appears: rounds in combat, minutes of game time. The first one to run out ends it. 0 = no limit.
PZone.EveryHint: Out of combat, the pace of effects set to "every N seconds".
PZone.TouchHint: Allies and enemies are read from the tokens' disposition (friendly, neutral, hostile), relative to the caster.
PZone.EffectsHint: For each effect: what happens in combat and out of combat (on entering, each turn inside, both, or nothing), and whether it is removed when leaving the zone. Unchecked, the effect keeps its own duration. "Only if" is computed on the target's sheet.
PZone.NoNatureWarn: "{name}": the zone has no nature, it is not placed (item's Zone tab).
PZone.NoGM: No GM connected: the zone cannot be placed.
PZone.NoShape: "{name}": the zone's area template is empty or not found (item's Zone tab).
PZone.NoPlace: The zone has nowhere to go (no aimed point, no target, no caster token).
PZone.CreateFailed: The zone could not be created (see the F12 console).
PZone.PowerHint: Two opposite natures never stay in the same place: the stronger one erases the other. Example: a water zone (power 4) placed on a fire (power 3) puts it out and takes its place.
PZone.PowerFieldHint: A number or a formula of the item, computed when placed (dice allowed).
PZone.EndPowerHint: Power drops steadily down to this share over the zone's duration. 100 = does not fade.
PZone.Shrink: Size drops with power (except zones attached to a token)
PZone.ExcludesHint: Separated by commas. One of the two zones excluding the other is enough.
PZone.Weaker_weaken: Does not appear, but weakens it
PZone.Overlap: Two zones of the same nature that touch
PZone.OverlapHint: Two gas grenades in the same place: one dose, two doses, or a single bigger cloud.
PZone.RepeatHint: For "On entering" effects: is a token that leaves and comes back struck again? Out of combat, "once per round" means once per interval.
PZone.ExclLose: "{name}" is stronger: the zone does not appear.
PZone.ExclWeaken: "{name}" is stronger: the zone does not appear, but weakens it.
PZone.ExclBoth: Same power as "{name}": both zones disappear.
PZone.MergeHint: Two zones of the same nature that touch become a single zone, with both shapes joined. It keeps the settings (effects, who is affected, look) of the strongest; at equal power, the older one's. Never for a zone attached to a token.
PZone.LookHint: What players see and hear. The zone's images, videos and sounds are set in the item's Media tab.
PZone.ColorHint: On the map (it has no light or dark theme: a single color).
PZone.Announce_chat: Chat message when someone is affected
PZone.BlockSightHint: A token inside the zone is hidden from those who don't own it (the GM sees everything). To also reduce the vision of the one inside, give them a "while inside" effect.
PZone.MediaWhere: Images, videos and sounds: the item's Media tab, "Zone" part.
PZone.MediaHint: What is seen WHILE the zone exists (flames, smoke, liquid): an image or video fills the zone under the tokens (if several, one is picked at random). With an image, the zone has no hatching, only its outline. It fades if the zone weakens. Transparent-background videos (webm) look best.
PZone.MediaAdd: Add an image or a video
PZone.StartSound: Sound on appearing (once, for the whole table)
PZone.TraceHint: An image stays on the ground (scorch mark, crater, puddle…): when the zone ends (end of duration, or driven out by an opposed zone) and / or on impact. It does nothing, it is just seen. A zone the GM erases by hand leaves no trace.
PZone.TraceHintNoZone: Even without a zone, the item can leave an image on the ground on impact (explosion crater, bullet hole…). It does nothing, it is just seen.
PZone.TraceEnd: Leaves a trace when the zone ends
PZone.TraceRotate: Randomly rotated (no two traces look the same)
PZone.TraceMediaWhere: Trace images: the item's Media tab, "Ground trace" part.
PZone.TraceNoMedia: No trace image: add some in the Media tab, otherwise nothing appears.
PZone.TraceMediaTitle: Ground trace — after the zone or on impact
PZone.TraceMediaHint: What STAYS on the ground (scorch mark, crater, puddle) when the zone ends or on impact, per the Zone tab. If several, one is picked at random for each trace.
PZone.CopyFrom: Copy the zone of another item…
PZone.CopyNone: No other world item leaves a zone or a trace.
PZone.CopyHint: All the zone settings of "{name}" (zone, appearance, trace, images and sounds) are replaced by those of the chosen item.
PZone.CopyOwnFx: The effects of "{name}" itself are not copied: pick them again (marked ⚠).
PZone.MergeLook_stretch: One image stretched over the whole
PZone.MergeLookHint: An effect image (flames, video) looks better piece by piece; a ground texture can be stretched over the whole zone.
PZone.FxLeaveHint: Checked: the effect goes away as soon as you leave the zone (smoke, aura). Unchecked: it keeps its own duration (burn).

WhenCalm.both: On entering, then every N seconds

PZone.EndWithEffectHint: For an aura attached to the caster: if the caster loses an effect this zone gave them (removed by hand, duration over…), the zone disappears.

Vision.OnlyOne: {actor}: only one vision can count at a time — "{name}" replaces the previous one.

Light.OptLightHint: Adds the "Light" tab to the item: the sight and light it gives its bearer, and its battery. Unchecking keeps the settings.
Light.Inherited: Set on the world item "{name}": its copies follow it.
Light.RemoveConfirm: This item's light settings will be deleted.
Light.ActivationHint: When the item gives light. "Only if": a formula read on the item (default "allume", the box toggled by the template's On / Off button). Empty: always.
Light.AutonomyOn: The item runs down while lit
Light.AutonomyHint: A key of the item (gauge or number) goes down in game time, only while it gives light. Add "key > 0" to "Only if" so it turns off at zero.
Light.TabHint: This item gives light and/or changes its bearer's sight. Fields accept a number or a formula read on the item (its condition, a value…). Its copies follow these settings.
Light.FormulaHint: Range, angle (1 to 360) and intensity (-1 to 1): a number or a formula read on the item.

Checker.Title: Template check
Checker.MenuHint: Searches the whole world for missing keys, broken references and formulas in error.
Checker.KeyMissingHere: Key "{key}" not found in this template.
Checker.ButtonMissing: Button "{key}" not found in item templates.
Checker.OnLoadIntro: Problems were found in this world's templates and settings. Each line says where; the button at the right of a group opens the matching window.
Checker.IgnoreThese: Don't warn me about these problems again
Checker.Legend: Error: this setting cannot work. Warning: a formula reads a key no template has (it will be 0 or empty).
Checker.RenameOthers: Other templates also have a key "{key}"
Checker.RenameOthersHint: Checked, they are renamed too. Unchecked, they keep the old key: shared settings (effects, HUD, managers…) will no longer read them.
Checker.RenameValues: Values already entered on sheets and items follow the new key.
Checker.FamCalMoonPhase: moon phases of the active calendar

Group.MembersHint: Drop character sheets here (owned by a player).
Group.NoMembers: No members: drop a character sheet here.
Group.BadMember: Only character sheets owned by a player can join a group.
Group.AlreadyMember: This character is already in the group.
Group.SavesHint: Each save keeps, for every member, their sheet, items and effects, with the world time. On load, everything returns to that moment (world time included); an item or effect that no longer exists in the world is left out.
Group.OverwriteConfirm: {slot} already holds a save. Overwrite it?
Group.LoadConfirm: Load {slot}? The members' sheets, items and effects return to that moment, and so does the world time.
Group.ActiveHint: Only one active group at a time: the auto save fills its auto slot.
Group.AutoTimerHint: 0 = never. Counted by the connected GM.
Group.Removed: Left out (no longer in the world):

Quest.PlainSheet: This quest is read in the “{sheet}” sheet: choose it in this journal's sheet configuration.
Quest.SubTabDeleteQuests: Its {n} quest(s) are not deleted: they stay in "All", with no tab.
Quest.DropSection: Drop a group or a PC here to create a section
Quest.StartHint: Create a section (drop a group or a PC on the left), then add a quest to it.
Quest.PlacePh: A place, or drop a scene or a journal
Quest.OptionalHint: An optional objective is not required to complete the quest.
Quest.DropActorHint: Drop a group or a character.
Quest.SectionIsGroup: This section follows a group: add the PC to the group.
Quest.SectionsHint: One section per group: each player only sees the quests of their characters' sections. Drop a group (its members follow) or chosen PCs; dropping a PC on a section adds it.
Quest.DelSectionConfirm: Delete the section "{name}"? Its {n} quest(s) stay in the journal, without a section (visible to the GM only).
Quest.RewardStatsHint: The sheet keys a quest can change (experience, money…) and how: add, remove or set the value.
Quest.IconHint: Font Awesome class, e.g. fa-solid fa-coins
Quest.StatusesHint: The four base statuses (padlock) can be renamed but not deleted. An added status chooses what it means: in progress, completed, failed or cancelled.
Quest.WidgetPlayers: Each player chooses (all tracked by default)
Quest.WidgetGm: The GM chooses (all tracked by default)
Quest.WidgetHint: "Quests in progress" button in the left bar (token controls). The GM sees every quest in progress there, section by section.
Quest.AutoCompleteHint: When all required objectives are done, the quest is completed and the rewards are distributed.

Confirm.success: The quest "{name}" is completed: distribute the rewards?
Confirm.fail: The quest "{name}" failed: apply the penalties?
Confirm.cancel: Cancel the quest "{name}"? Nothing is distributed.

Quest.AutoCheckHint: Checked as soon as the formula is true for a member (or for the target, or one of its tokens).
Quest.AutoCountHint: The counter takes the sum of the formula over the members (on the target: the highest value), up to the number to reach.
Quest.RevealIfHint: The quest is hidden: it appears when the GM clicks the eye, on "Announce", through a button's "Quest" step (Give), or as soon as this formula is true for a member of the section (it is then announced).
Quest.TrackerEmpty: No tracked quest. A revealed quest shows up here; the journal's pin removes or restores it.
Quest.TrackerNone: No quest in progress in this section.
Quest.TrackerNoSection: No section: create one in a quest journal.

Prop.Opt: Scene object (can be placed on the map)
Prop.CfgHint: DEFAULT values for items of this template: each world item can change them in its “Scene” tab. Placed on the scene, the item becomes a token that keeps the whole item (values, state, slot contents). Double-click opens its panel: its “once placed” buttons, used by the interacting character.
Prop.SizeHint: In cells, in pixels, or the real image size (both numbers are then ignored).
Prop.RangeHint: Maximum distance between the character's token and the item, edge to edge. 0 = no limit. The GM is never limited.
Prop.StateHint: Optional: an item key, then one line per value "value = image path" (lever up / down, vein full / depleted).
Prop.HpHint: Optional: the key (gauge or number) of the item's HP. At 0: destroyed, or dropped on the ground there.
Prop.WhereHint: For a scene object: “once placed”, the button appears in the placed item's panel (double-click), and the interacting character is its user (their rolls, what is taken from them; the item's contents stay its own). “Auto”: once placed if the item is deployable (“Scene object” option and its condition), otherwise in the inventory.
Prop.Aim: Click to place (right-click or Esc: cancel).
Prop.NotProp: This item cannot be placed on the scene (its template's “Scene object” option, or its condition).
Prop.Failed: The item could not be placed or picked up.
Prop.TooFar: Too far: move your token closer.
Prop.NotYours: Only whoever placed it can use it.
Prop.TabHintWorld: Settings of THIS item once placed on the scene. An empty field keeps the template's default (gear of the “Scene object” option). Its copies (inventories, placed) follow these settings.
Prop.TabHintCopy: Settings specific to THIS copy. An empty field follows the world item “{name}”.
Prop.IgnoreCombatHint: Checked: the item cannot be targeted, no attack or area hits it, it never joins the combat tracker. Unchecked: it can be attacked — its defense and resistances are read on the item (same keys as on a sheet), damage goes to its hit point key below.
Prop.AimOrient: Orientation: move the mouse around the point (Shift: free, wheel: fine tuning), click to confirm; right-click or Esc: cancel.
Prop.OnlyPlaced: Usable once placed on the scene.
Prop.MustStayProp: {name} is placed on the scene: it must remain a scene object. Take it back first to change that.
Prop.FireArcHint: For a placed item that attacks (turret, cannon…): the target, aimed point or area must lie within this arc, centered on the item's front (the top of its image, which turns with it). The arc is shown while aiming. 0 = all around.
Prop.PropIfHint: Optional: a formula read on the item. Only items that satisfy it are scene objects (Scene tab, placing). A placed item cannot stop satisfying it while it is on the scene.
Prop.Where_auto: once placed if deployable, otherwise in the inventory
Prop.OnlyInstalled: Usable once installed on the scene.
Prop.Salvaged: {name} is dismantled: its contents are taken.

Panel.Hint: What double-clicking the placed item shows. Build it with the usual components; "Template component" shows a component already on the sheet (same key, same value: nothing is copied). Empty: an automatic panel with the "once placed" buttons. Fields are read-only there; you act through the buttons.
Panel.Empty: No component: the automatic panel will be used.
Panel.RefTargetHint: A template component (sheet or tab): it is also shown here, with its value and visibility rules.
Panel.Head: Header
Panel.HeadOpt: Show the header (item image and name)
Panel.RefNoLabelHint: The component is shown without its label. Otherwise: the label entered above, or, if empty, the component's own.

Tile.Drop: Drop a world item (scene object) here to attach it to this tile.
Tile.DropReplace: Drop another world item to replace it.
Tile.Hint: The tile becomes this item: double-click, triggers, panel, buttons. An invisible token is placed over it; the item's image-by-key changes the tile's image. You can also drop the world item on the tile, on the map.
Tile.NotProp: {name} is not a "scene object" world item.
Tile.IsModel: {name} is a template: create a world item with this template, then drop that item.
Tile.DropAsk: {name} was dropped on a decor tile. Attach it to this tile, install it here, or drop it on the ground?
Tile.MoveTile: This item is attached to a tile: move the tile (Tiles layer), the item follows.

Region.Drop: Drop a world item (scene object) here to attach it to this region.
Region.DropReplace: Drop another world item to replace it.
Region.Hint: The item is placed at the center of the region (its image, its size): double-click, triggers, panel, buttons. A trap uses the region's shape as its trigger zone. You can also drop the world item onto the region, on the map.
Region.DropAsk: {name} was dropped on a region. Attach it to this region, install it here, or drop it on the ground?
Region.MoveRegion: This item is attached to a region: edit the region (regions layer), the item follows.

DoorProp.Drop: Drop a world item (scene object) here to attach it to this door.
DoorProp.DropReplace: Drop another world item to replace it.
DoorProp.Hint: Clicking the door opens the item's panel instead of opening the door: its buttons open or close the door ("Scene → Door" step, the door is already in its links). The GM keeps right-click to lock.
DoorProp.NotDoor: This wall is not a door.
DoorProp.MoveDoor: This item is attached to a door: move the wall (walls layer), the item follows.

Trig.DblClickHint: Unchecked, players do not open the panel by double-click (the GM still does).
Trig.ApproachHint: When a character token reaches this distance (edge to edge, in cells), coming from farther away: stopping there, passing through (its path enters it), or both. The panel opens, or the chosen button runs, on behalf of that character. "Once": the GM re-arms it from the panel.
Trig.DropIf: Accepted items (formula on the dropped item)
Trig.DropHint: An item dropped from an inventory onto the placed item runs the chosen button, on behalf of its carrier; the dropped item becomes the chosen item of its steps (pickedName, picked_key). Empty formula: any item.

Scene.GroupStepPh: empty = all links of this type

OpName.salvage: Take its contents (the trap is destroyed)

Scene.NotPlaced: {name} must be placed on the scene to act on it.
Scene.NoLink: No linked element for "{group}" (GM: Scene links, at the panel footer).
Scene.NoPanel: No placed item with a panel among the links (item token, or tile, door, region with an attached item).
Scene.PickHint: Click a door, light, sound, tile, token, drawing or region (Escape or right-click: cancel).
Scene.PickNone: Nothing here: click a door, light, sound, tile, token, drawing or region.
Scene.LinksHint: The scene elements this item controls (its "Scene" steps). Give them a group to target them separately ("north door", "alarm").

Traces.Title: Ground traces
Traces.MenuHint: Blood, mud, oil…: the stains left by characters who are hit or who move.
Traces.MaxPerSceneHint: Beyond that, the oldest disappear (a crowded scene slows the display).
Traces.Name: Name
Traces.DeleteConfirm: Delete the trace type "{name}"? Traces already placed stay until cleaned.
Traces.ConditionHint: Pick the key (e.g. hp), then the condition: "< 80" in "% of maximum" = wounded below 80% of their health. "Always" = on every move.
Traces.ScaleTokenHint: Splats, footprints and step spacing grow with the token: a 2×2 token leaves traces twice as big as a 1×1 token.
Traces.TrackHint: For "hidden" types. The magnifier button in the left bar rolls the roll set on this key (selected token's sheet); on success, hidden traces around the token appear for that player. The GM always sees them.
Traces.HoverAgeHint: Hovering a trace shows its type and how long it has been there (world time). For the GM, and for a player on traces they tracked.
Traces.WhenHint: Alternating steps: one foot per step (left, right…) instead of a pair. None when flying: no traces while the token flies, swims, burrows or teleports (Foundry movement action). Hidden: only the GM sees them, players must track them.
Traces.DragHint: While the condition is true (e.g. hp ≤ 0), the moved token leaves a long continuous drag mark instead of its steps: a wounded body being dragged.
Traces.ImpactOn: Stains when the watched key drops
Traces.ImpactHint: A stain on each drop of the key; with a condition, only when it holds after the hit (e.g. < 50% of maximum). The bigger the loss, the bigger the stains. The delay lets a shot animation finish.
Traces.TrailOn: A trail when the character moves
Traces.TrailHint: For footprints, use the "Footprints" shape and check "facing".
Traces.ColorKeyHint: Key of a Color component on the template: each character has its own color; without a key, the default color.
Traces.BloodKeyHint: Blood always reads the fixed key "blood": put a Color component with the key blood on the template to give each character its blood color.
Traces.WallsHint: A door counts as it is when the stain appears: open, the trace goes through; closed, it stops. The shape then stays fixed.
Traces.NoType: No trace type: add one, or restore the original blood.
Traces.ClearWhat: Which traces to erase from this scene?
Traces.TemplatesHint: Check the templates that leave this trace (e.g. human blood on one side, alien blood on the other). None checked = all. Exception for one character: its color key (blood for blood) still takes priority.

traceType.label: Trace type
traceType.hint: The trace left by tokens in this region (Settings → Configure traces).

mode.label: When
mode.hint: On the region: while walking inside (snow). On exit: for a few cells after leaving (mud on the feet). Weather: the region leaves nothing, it erases the traces inside it.

cases.label: On exit: for (squares)
cases.hint: Number of squares during which tokens still leave traces after the region.

eraseAfter.label: Weather: erased after (game hours)
eraseAfter.hint: Weather mode: traces inside the region disappear after this much game time (rain, falling snow, tide).

Traces.FootprintHint: Click a footprint: it is this type's print when no rule in the "Footprints" section targets the character.
Traces.FpHint: Who leaves which footprint, for every trace type (the type gives the color, the rule gives the shape). The first matching rule wins: put the most specific ones on top. No rule → the type's default footprint. Key with "Always": as soon as the key has a value; a text value is compared ignoring case (race = elf).
Traces.FpNone: No rule: each type uses its default footprint.
Traces.ByLoss: More stains when the loss is heavy
Traces.ImagesHint: Images (one by one or a whole folder) are added to the ticked shapes of BOTH impact and trail, rotated, mirrored and tinted with the trace color: prefer light (white or grey) images on a transparent background.
Traces.LookHint: Footprints, images and color are shared by impact and trail; shapes are ticked in each section.
Traces.TrailGrow: Bigger and bigger as the key drops (in % of its maximum)
Traces.EffectsHint: Optional. Ticked: the trace also (or only) happens when the character has one of these effects — Bleeding, for instance. Nothing ticked: the option is not used.

name.label: Station name
name.hint: E.g. forge, workbench, laboratory. Formulas test it with atStation("forge"); atStation() = any station.

Bars.MenuHint: Bars shown on tokens: for all characters, per template, or per token.
Bars.Title: Token bars
Bars.AllHint: These bars show on every character, except for a template that has its own bars. A token can then change, hide or add bars (token configuration, Resources tab).
Bars.TplHint: "Follows All": the bars of "All characters". "Own bars": only this template's. "All + own": both. They travel with the template export.
Bars.PickOrAdd: Pick a bar, or add one.
Bars.Label: Name
Bars.LabelHint: To find it in the list; it can also show on the bar (prefix, Text tab).
Bars.ValueHint: A template key (hp) or a formula (hp + shield).
Bars.MaxHint: Empty: the maximum of the key's gauge (or bounded number).
Bars.InvertHint: Invert: the bar is full when the value is 0 (stress, hunger, fatigue…).
Bars.HudEditHint: A field in the token HUD to change the value by hand ("12", "+5", "-3"), for the GM only or also the owner. Only when the value is an entered key (not computed). The gauge bounds apply.
Bars.RowHint: 0 = against the token's edge; bars on the same row share the width.
Bars.Smooth: The bar slides when the value changes
Bars.TermForHint: For example: the GM sees "12 / 47", players only see "Wounded" on an enemy.
Bars.ApproxHint: For those who don't see the numbers: the bar moves in steps (5 = by fifths). 0 = exact value.
Bars.VisibleIfHint: Optional formula on the sheet; also value, max, min and pct (0 to 100).
Bars.StepsHint: The first matching step applies: color, pattern, animation, term, sound when reached.
Bars.TokenBoxHint: Bars inherited from "All" and the template. This token only saves what you change.
Bars.TokenNone: No SBE bars for this character.
Bars.TokenPatchHint: Only the settings you change here are kept for this token; the rest always follows the template.
Bars.TokenExtraHint: A bar that only exists on this token.
Bars.OverridesHint: SBE bars are set in their own window (for all, per sheet template, per token). They don't depend on "Display Bars" below, which only concerns Foundry's bars.
Bars.BrawlTitle: Token bars: Bar Brawl is active
Bars.BrawlWarn: Bar Brawl is active: SBE bars are paused. SBE bars do everything Bar Brawl does, and more (formulas, steps, animations, per-template setup); we recommend disabling it.
Bars.ImagesHint: Your own images (PNG, SVG, WebP…). The shape cuts the bar; the frame sits on top and stretches without distorting its edges.
Bars.MaskImageHint: A white image on a transparent background: the bar takes its shape (diamond, syringe, skull…). Replaces the shape chosen above.
Bars.FrameImageHint: An image placed over the bar (frame, rivets, ornaments). Its edges stay sharp, only the middle stretches.
Bars.FrameSliceHint: The width, in image pixels, of the edges that don't stretch. Caps make the frame extend at both ends (icon, cap…).
Bars.HudGapHint: The field always goes after the bars placed outside on that side; the distance is added (negative = closer).
Bars.ImportBad: This file contains no SBE token bars.
Bars.FloatOn: Floating values (−12 / +5) when the value changes
Bars.TextStepColor: Step color (its effect color, else its color)
Bars.ImportOne: Replace this bar from a file
Bars.OffsetHint: Moves the bar away from the token (positive) or closer (negative), along the chosen edge.

Looks.Title: Token looks
Looks.ReloadHint: Read the folder again after adding or removing images.
Looks.Count: {n} image(s) in this folder. The HUD button appears from 2 images.
Looks.FolderHint: One folder per character: each image is a look of its token (outfits, forms…). The sheet portrait does not change.
Looks.OwnerSees: The owner also sees the true face under a disguise
Looks.ImagesHint: Everything is optional: empty = the prototype token setting. Size in squares, image scale, name shown on the token. Disguise: the GM sees the true look instead (the one picked by hand, else the default one).
Looks.Label: Label
Looks.Name: Displayed name
Looks.RulesHint: The first matching rule wins; when none matches any more, the token goes back to the look picked by hand (else the default one).

Trap.GroupHint: Tick “This is a trap”: the placed item watches its trigger zone. Everything is set here; the person placing it only places it, turns it and places its zone.
Trap.trZoneHint: The item's own space, a radius around it, a rectangle, or a circle / cone (angle < 360) facing the top of the item.
Trap.trPlaceHint: Rectangle or circle / cone: the zone follows the mouse (wheel = rotate), a click places it. Otherwise it is centered on the item.
Trap.trResizeHint: When placing: a rectangle is drawn in two clicks (its two corners); a circle or cone first asks for its radius and angle.
Trap.trHiddenHint: Visible only to the GM, to whoever placed it and to players whose character spotted it. Whoever placed it never triggers it.
Trap.trDetDcHint: Formula read on the trap: makes the roll harder (empty or 0 = the roll as is).
Trap.trLastHint: Not spotted yet: one last detection roll when entering; on success, the character steps back.
Trap.trBtnHint: A “once placed” button of the item: its target is the character who triggered it (attack, zone centered on them or from the trap towards them, effect…).

Z.Title: Zone size
Z.Place: Zone: place it (wheel = rotate, Shift = fine), click to confirm. Escape or right click: cancel.

Trap.Speaker: Trap
Trap.NotTrap: This item is not a trap.
Trap.OtherScene: A character moves on scene “{scene}”, which has traps: view that scene so they can trigger.
Trap.trDodgeIfHint: Read on the trap, e.g. a “dodgeable” checkbox; empty = always.
Trap.NoRoll: Key “{key}” has no dice roll: set a roll on that field of the character template.
Trap.trAlliesHint: Characters with the same disposition as whoever placed it.
Trap.trDetKeyHint: Roll key of the character passing by.
Trap.trAvoidHint: A character who spotted it walks past without triggering it.
Trap.trDodgeKeyHint: Roll key of the character who triggers it; empty = no dodge.
Trap.trDodgeDcHint: Formula read on the trap: makes the roll harder (empty or 0 = the roll as is).
Trap.trCenterHint: Where the button's effect area is centered when the trap fires: on the trap (fixed trap: mine, pit…) or on the victim.
Trap.trDisarmKeyHint: Dice-roll key of the character who disarms (empty = no roll). Disarmed: harmless, visible to everyone, and it can be picked up.
Trap.trDisarmDcHint: Formula read on the trap, making the roll harder (empty = none).
Trap.ShowZones: Trap areas (trigger in yellow, effect in red)
Trap.ShareHint: Tick the characters who know where it is: they see it and avoid it. You always see it.

Ask.Title: Window title
Ask.Label: Question
Ask.ChoicesPh:
value = displayed text
e.g. short = Short burst
Ask.BadKey: "{key}": a question's name uses lowercase letters, digits and _, and starts with a letter.

Auto.Title: Runs by itself
Auto.Hint: The button fires without a click when an event happens. Character button: its own events. Item button: its carrier's (depending on the scope), or its own when placed. It runs on the character's player's client if connected (their windows), otherwise on the GM's. Its steps read eventName (the event, signal, effect, watched value or the target brought to 0), eventValue (damage or healing amount) and eventSource (who sent the signal).

Ev.equip: Equipped (put in a slot or an "equipped" container)

Auto.NeedFormula: "A formula becomes true": write the formula.
Auto.WatchKeyPh: key; empty = the one that takes damage
Auto.DropHint: Runs right before the write: eventValue = the expected drop. The new drop is kept between 0 and the expected drop, then the steps follow (without "Ask first"). Typing directly in the sheet triggers nothing.

Cond.NotHint: Inverts this sentence (it must be false).

ModeTail.all: of these conditions must be true
ModeTail.any: of these conditions must be true

Cond.AdvancedHint: Checked: conditions are written as formulas, as before. Unchecked: they are built as sentences (“ammo” “is greater than” “0”). The formula stays the same; this setting is yours only.

Languages.Title: Character languages
Languages.MenuHint: Your world's languages: a passage written in a language is scrambled for the player whose character does not know it.
Languages.ViewAsHint: Read texts and chat as this character would. This setting is yours only.
Languages.DeleteConfirm: Delete the language “{name}”? Marked passages will become readable for everyone.
Languages.HowTo: To mark a passage: in a text editor (journal, description, note), select the passage then click the “Language” button of the toolbar.
Languages.Name: Name
Languages.ModeHint: What someone who does not understand a word sees. Length and punctuation are kept.
Languages.AlphabetHint: The signs used instead of letters, stuck together (runes, ideograms…).
Languages.FontHint: A strange script for the words not understood (Foundry's fonts and yours).
Languages.ShowNameHint: Unchecked: someone who does not know the language at all sees “Unknown language”.
Languages.ChatHint: Characters who know it can choose it next to the chat input; their messages are then read according to each reader's mastery.
Languages.DecipherOnHint: Clicking a scrambled passage makes this roll; on a success, this passage becomes fully readable for this character, for good.
Languages.DecipherOnceHint: A failure closes this passage for this character.
Languages.DecipherKeyHint: A rollable field of the character sheet (skill, intelligence…).
Languages.DecipherDiffHint: Makes the roll harder, like the difficulty of the roll window. Read on the character.
Languages.PreviewText: The key is hidden under the third stone of the old well, on the north side.
Languages.NoRoll: The roll “{key}” does not exist on this character.
Languages.SpeakLabel: Your chat messages are said in
Languages.KeyHint: A component with the same key on the character sheet grants the language: a Number gives the mastery % (100 = reads everything, 40 = 40% of the words, always the same ones for them), a checked Checkbox counts as 100%. Items and effects can raise it through their contributions (an equipped translator). Advanced: a formula is accepted too.
Languages.KeyMissing: Without a key, nobody knows this language.
Languages.KeyUnknown: No character template has a “{key}” component yet: add a Number or a Checkbox with this key.

Ph.ChartAxes:
str_mod : STR
con_mod : CON
dex_mod : DEX : #b5471f
Ph.GiveWhere: key; empty = the first container that accepts it

Unid.CfgHint: While the key below is false on an item, players see its unknown version (name, image, description set by the GM on the item: its sheet's ⋮ menu → “Identification options”). The GM always sees the real item.
Unid.KeyHint: A checkbox of the item. A button that checks it identifies the item (with a roll, a skill…); the GM can also do it with a right click in the inventory.
Unid.Group: Identifying one copy identifies all copies of the same item
Unid.GroupHint: All “Red potion” vials are recognized as soon as one is (for every character).
Unid.DlgHint: What players see while the item is unknown. Uncheck to identify it (a button or the “Identify” right click do it too). Set on the world item, its copies follow it.
Unid.Name: Name seen by players
Unid.ByModel: Its template sets this for all its items (key “{key}”).
Unid.MakeUnknown: Make this item unknown to players

Wait.SettingGround: Waiting items: offer "Drop on the ground"
Wait.SettingGroundHint: In the window of items received without room (full container, full spatial grid), the player can drop them on the ground.
Wait.Title: Waiting items: {name}
Wait.Hint: These items have no room yet. Make room in your inventory and drag them into a container, or choose what to do with them.
Wait.AllStored: Every item has found its place.
Wait.NoOwner: The former owner cannot be found.

Init.Title: Initiative
Init.Hint: The combatants' initiative roll. A template that has the given field uses it; otherwise the formula. One line per template overrides this setting for that template.
Init.KeyHint: A sheet field. If it has a configured roll, that roll is made (its formula, bonuses, criticals, visibility). Without a roll, its value is the initiative score, with no dice.
Init.FormulaHint: Used when the template has no such field. Dice and sheet keys allowed.
Init.ModelsHint: Optional: a template that rolls something else (creatures, vehicles…).
Init.AskHint: Only when a single combatant is rolled by hand (never for "roll all" nor the round reroll). With a roll field, the options are that field's window options.
Init.WindowHint: These options and the visibility below apply to the formula. A hidden combatant always rolls privately for the GM.
Init.TieHint: Formula read on the sheet at roll time: the highest goes first. Empty: no tie-breaker.
Init.PassesHint: At the end of a pass, each score drops by the step; those still above the minimum act again in the same round. On the next round, the original score comes back (or is rerolled).
Init.Min: Minimum to act again (number or formula)
Init.AutoHint: When "Begin Combat" is clicked, those without a score roll without a window, then combat starts in the right order. A combatant who joins a combat already under way also rolls on their own.

Summon.WhileEffect: While the summoner has the effect
Summon.CasterDown: They leave if the summoner drops to 0
Summon.Hint: Each creature is a copy (unlinked token), aimed on the map. Without a duration: until dismissed. Formulas read summoned() (the character's summons) or summoned("Name").
Summon.Missing: The creature to summon no longer exists.
Summon.ValuesHint: Written on each creature when it arrives, over the NPC's own. Formulas read the item, carrier("key") for the summoner and answers from earlier steps; dice are rolled for each creature. E.g. hp = replace carrier("level") * 10.

Loc.MenuHint: Bodies and their zones (head, arms…): odds, effect on damage, drawing to aim at.
Loc.SectionHint: Bodies and their zones are set in their own window. Each attack profile (or weapon) says where the hit zone comes from, under "Hit location".
Loc.PickOrCreate: Pick a body, or create one.
Loc.Name: Name
Loc.ModelsHint: The character templates that use this body. A body with no template is used by all the others (default body). A template has only one body.
Loc.NoModels: No character template in this world.
Loc.ZonesHint: By ranges: the drawn value (separate roll or read from the attack roll) gives the zone. By area: the bigger the zone on the drawing, the more often it is hit. Empty box = the normal rule: the Combat manager's damage key, no extra protection, ×1, no modifier. Later steps read hitZone ("Right arm" → right_arm).
Loc.ZonePick: Draw in this zone (a selected piece moves into it)
Loc.DrawingHint: Each drawn piece belongs to the marked zone; a zone can have several. Select tool: pick a piece, drag it; then clicking a zone's dot moves it there. The drawing is used to aim (aimed shot), to show the hit zone in the card, and for odds by area.
Loc.NeedRange: {body}: the zone "{name}" has no range (From, To).
Loc.NeedDrawing: {body}: with odds by area, each zone must be drawn.
Loc.DupModel: The template "{template}" is in two bodies: {a} and {b}.
Loc.TwoDefaults: Only one body can have no template (default body).
Loc.ImportDone: Import: {added} added, {replaced} replaced. Check, then Save.
Loc.AimAsk: Click the aimed zone on the target's silhouette, or roll at random.

After.Group: After the roll: rerolls and bonuses
After.GroupHint: Buttons to improve a roll by paying a resource from the sheet (luck, heroism…), or for free. Roll with nothing after it (sheet label, HUD, last step of a button): on its card, which updates. Roll followed by something else (step button, attack, lock…): a window right after the dice, before what follows. "Reroll damage" (a weapon's roll field): a button under each target's damage in the attack card, areas included; damage already applied is corrected. No action = nothing after the roll.
After.Label: Label
After.NeedValue: "{label}": the value (dice or bonus) is required.
After.NoUses: No more uses for this roll
After.NoFailed: No failed die (only for dice pools counted in successes)
After.Title: After the roll
After.Gone: This attack's item no longer exists.

Cal.MenuHint: The world's calendars (one active), weather types, date display and scene options.
Cal.Title: Calendar
Cal.NoCalendar: No calendar. The GM creates one in Calendar setup.
Cal.NewBaseHint: A complete calendar (months, days, seasons, moon) to adapt.
Cal.DeleteConfirm: Delete the calendar "{name}" and its events?
Cal.ImportDone: Import done: {n} calendar(s). Remember to save.
Cal.ImportBad: Unreadable file, or not an SBE calendars export.
Cal.GeneralHint: Foundry's game time (in seconds) is split by this calendar: length of minutes, hours and days. Changing them shifts dates already written.
Cal.Name: Name
Cal.YearZeroHint: The year shown when game time is 0. Years are counted from it.
Cal.FirstWeekdayHint: The weekday of the very first day (time 0): it sets all the others.
Cal.LeapEveryHint: 0: never. 4: one year in four uses its months' "leap days".
Cal.MonthsHint: Months in order. "Leap days": the month's length in a leap year (empty = the same).
Cal.DaysHint: Weekdays in order. The abbreviation is used in the calendar grid.
Cal.SeasonsHint: Each season starts on a date and lasts until the next one. It sets temperatures, the sun and the possible weather.
Cal.TempRangeHint: In °C. Each day draws its temperature in this range; nights are cooler, and each weather type adds its offset.
Cal.SeasonWeatherHint: The possible types and their weight: the higher the weight, the more frequent the type. No line: the world's first type.
Cal.NoSeasonWeather: No weather: the world's first type will be used.
Cal.NoSeasons: No season: default temperatures and sun.
Cal.MoonsHint: Each moon runs on a cycle (in days). "Offset": the day (from time zero) of its first new moon.
Cal.WeatherHint: The world's weather types, shared by all calendars. Each type: an icon, a temperature offset, an SBE effect, a Foundry scene effect, and a sky drawn in layers.
Cal.AddBaseHint: Adds back the missing built-in types (nature, fantasy, science fiction).
Cal.TempModHint: Added (in °C) to the day's temperature while this weather lasts.
Cal.WxEffectHint: Applied to the characters of the active scene's tokens while this weather lasts (except indoor scenes), removed afterwards.
Cal.SceneFxHint: What every player sees on the active scene while this weather lasts ("Weather on the active scene" option, except indoor scenes). Layers add up: recolored Foundry effects and SBE effects.
Cal.SkyHint: Without its own sky, the sky follows the hour (dawn, day, dusk, night). With one: two colors by day, two by night.
Cal.LayersHint: Tick what is drawn in the dome; the preview above updates. Colors appear for the ticked layers.
Cal.DisplayHint: Each player can change these formats for themselves from the calendar.
Cal.OptPlayers: Players see the clock and the calendar
Cal.OptAutoWeatherHint: Drawn by season at each slot. Unchecked: only the weather the GM sets counts.
Cal.OptSceneWeatherHint: Sets the current type's Foundry scene effect (except indoor scenes).
Cal.OptSceneDarkness: The hour sets the active scene's darkness
Cal.OptSceneDarknessHint: Dark at night, bright by day, one hour of transition at sunrise and sunset (except indoor scenes).
Cal.IndoorScenes: Indoor scenes: no weather, no darkness
Cal.IndoorScenesHint: Tick only sheltered scenes (buildings, underground…): weather, darkness and the weather effect don't apply there. Unticked scenes get the weather.
Cal.WeatherHold: Keep until further notice (otherwise: until tomorrow)
Cal.LinkGone: The linked document no longer exists.
Cal.EvLinkPh: Drop a quest, a journal, a scene… here
Cal.SettingEnabledHint: Enabled: the clock is always shown and the calendar opens at every launch (it can be closed). The GM sets the rest in "Set up the calendar".
Cal.ResetPos: Put the clock back in place (top slot)
Cal.CategoryHint: Groups this type in the weather menu and in this list. Free text: reuse an existing category or create one.
Cal.ResetMenuHint: On this computer: the clock goes back to the top slot, right of the scene navigation, and the calendar to its starting place. Useful if one of them went off screen.
Cal.ResetDone: Clock and calendar put back in place.
Cal.SceneNone: No effect: the scene stays as it is.
Cal.SettingSoundsHint: Plays the sounds of the scene's weather (rain, wind, thunder…). Volume is set with the "Environment" slider of the audio settings.
Cal.SoundsHint: Played for every player on the active scene (except indoors). "Loop": continuous, with a crossfade when the weather changes. "Random": comes back now and then. "On lightning": starts at the same instant as the scene's lightning; on each flash, one of these rows is drawn at random. A library entry holding several sounds draws one each time.
Cal.SoundGapHint: Wait between two plays (in seconds, drawn at random between these two values)
Cal.SoundBad: This sound is missing or unreadable.
Cal.KeySeasonHint: What formulas (season()) and action steps read. Lowercase, no accents or spaces. Renaming the season does not change it.
Cal.KeyWeatherHint: What formulas (weather()) and action steps read. Lowercase, no accents or spaces. Renaming the type does not change it.
Cal.KeyTwice: The key "{key}" is used twice: each weather type (and each season of a calendar) needs its own.
Cal.SoundDistHint: Each flash gets a random distance (the same for everyone): this row plays for every flash, close ones only, or distant ones only.
Cal.SoundDelayHint: Maximum delay (seconds): a flash far away is heard after this delay; a close one, at once.
Cal.SoundFadeHint: Volume drop at the farthest (%): a distant flash is quieter accordingly. 0: same volume everywhere.
Cal.MoonCycleHint: How long a full cycle of the moon lasts, in days (decimals allowed).
Cal.MoonOffsetHint: The day (from time zero) when the cycle starts: its first phase.
Cal.MoonColorHint: Color of the moon's text in the clock and calendar; a phase with its own color wins.
Cal.KeyMoonHint: What formulas (moon("key")) and action steps read. Lowercase, no accents or spaces.
Cal.PhasesHint: Phases follow the order of the list, each for its share of the cycle ("Length": 1 and 2 = the second lasts twice as long). The first is centered on the start of the cycle. A RARE phase (star) takes the place of another on some cycles: every N cycles and/or with a % chance (empty or 0 = never on that side). Each phase has its key (formulas moon(), moonPhase(), "phase change" trigger, "Moon" step) and can apply an SBE effect while it lasts.
Cal.PhaseLengthHint: Its share of the cycle (relative to the other phases). 0 everywhere: equal shares.
Cal.PhaseReplacesHint: The normal phase this one replaces on the cycles it shows up.
Cal.PhaseEveryHint: It comes back every N cycles (the Nth, the 2Nth…). 0 = no regular return.
Cal.PhaseChanceHint: Chance it shows up on each cycle (in %), drawn ahead of time, the same for everyone. 0 = no chance.
Cal.PhaseEffectHint: SBE effect applied to the characters of the active scene while this phase lasts (except indoor scenes).
Cal.ProvidedHint: Provided by SBE: its name (translated), icon and key cannot change; everything else can be set. For your own version, create one (or duplicate a weather).
Cal.AddBaseSeasonsHint: Puts back the missing base seasons (spring, summer, autumn, winter).
Cal.AddBaseMoonHint: Puts back the base moon, with its eight phases.
Cal.KeysMigrated: Calendar: {n} provided keys switched to English (e.g. clear, spring, full_moon); {docs} setting(s) updated. A formula comparing a text (weather() == "rain") must be fixed by hand.
Cal.CatMenuHide: Offered in the clock's weather menu — click to remove it
Cal.CatMenuShow: Missing from the clock's weather menu — click to add it

Inactive.CfgHint: Formula read on the item. While it is true, the item no longer gives anything to the sheet carrying it: its values no longer count in carried() (bonuses, imposed advantage, avoided critical failure). It stays in the inventory and carriedCount() still counts it. E.g. a skill from a class the character does not have.
Inactive.ImportApplied: "Inactive if" option of the imported template applied.

Undo.MenuHint: The table's latest actions: go back or redo.
Undo.SettingSizeHint: Number of actions kept (the oldest drop out).
Undo.Ask: Go back: {n} action(s) undone, from the most recent to this one:
Undo.GmOnly: Only the GM can undo an action.
Undo.Missed: ({n} change(s) could not be found and were left as they are.)
Undo.HistoryHint: Most recent at the top. "Go back here" undoes this action and all the ones after it; "Redo" brings undone actions back.
Undo.SettingOnHint: Records every action (button, attack, trigger) so the GM can undo it from its chat card. Unchecked: nothing is recorded and no card offers "Undo".

Talents.Empty: Empty tree: open its editor to place the nodes.
Talents.EditorHint: Double-click: new node. Drag a node's dot onto another: link (from parent to child). Drag the background: move the view. Delete: erase the selection.
Talents.Name: Name
Talents.RanksHint: More than one rank: the node unlocks in several steps (1/3, 2/3, 3/3).
Talents.SelectHint: Click a node or a link to set it up.
Talents.LoopRefused: This link would make a loop: a node cannot depend on itself.
Talents.HeightHint: The tree scrolls inside this area when it is bigger.
Talents.ComponentHint: The tree's layout is drawn with the "Edit tree" button, under the component in the workshop.
Talents.CostHint: Empty = 1. "rank" is the rank being bought (1, 2, 3…): "rank * 2" costs 2, then 4, then 6.
Talents.CondHint: Formula read on the sheet: the node is only available when it is true.
Talents.GroupHint: Nodes of the same group exclude each other: unlocking one closes the others.
Talents.PointsKeyHint: Key on the carrier's sheet the points are taken from (tree of an item: the sheet of whoever carries it).
Talents.ReqAny: At least one of these nodes:
Talents.ReqGroup: No other node of its group
Talents.WhyPending: Request sent to the GM, pending.
Talents.WhyParents: The parent nodes are not unlocked.
Talents.WhyCond: The sheet condition is not met.
Talents.WhyCost: Cost cannot be computed (check the formula).
Talents.WhyGm: Only the GM unlocks the nodes of this tree.
Talents.AskNote: {user} asks to unlock "{node}": see the chat.
Talents.Missing: This node or tree no longer exists.
Talents.Refund_both: Node by node and whole tree
Talents.RefundHint: Taking a rank back returns its points; a node another unlocked node depends on cannot be taken back.
Talents.RefundPctHint: Share of the paid points returned when taking back: 100 = all, 0 = none.
Talents.AskRefundBtn: Ask the GM to remove it
Talents.ResetConfirm: Every node of "{tree}" goes back to zero. Points returned: {back}. Continue?
Talents.WhyOwner: Only the sheet's owner can do this.
Talents.WhyNoRefund: This tree does not allow taking a node back.
Talents.WhyNoReset: This tree does not allow a reset.
Talents.WhyGmRefund: Only the GM takes back the nodes of this tree.
Talents.AskRefundText: {user} asks to remove a rank of "{node}" ({tree}).
Talents.AskRefundNote: {user} asks to remove "{node}": see the chat.
Talents.AskResetNote: {user} asks to reset "{node}": see the chat.
Talents.BonusHint: Counted when the value is computed, while the node is unlocked; "rank" is its rank ("rank * 2"). Hovering the value names the node.
Talents.BonusHintItem: Counted when computed, while the node is unlocked; "rank" is its rank. Each bonus targets the carrier's sheet or the item itself.
Talents.ButtonHint: An action button of the template (it may be hidden on the sheet), run at each unlocked rank.
Talents.ItemWorldOnly: Only a world item can be given (not a carried one).
Talents.RewardsBack: Items and effects when taken back
Talents.RewardsBackHint: When a rank is taken back: the given item and applied effect go away, or stay. Value bonuses always follow the node.
Talents.ColorsHint: One color per state; empty = SBE's color.

VisionModes.MenuHint: The world's vision modes: on-screen look, and soon what they let you spot.
VisionModes.Title: Vision modes
VisionModes.Builtin: Starting mode: can be renamed, tuned and reset.
VisionModes.Pick: Pick a mode on the left.
VisionModes.Name: Name
VisionModes.PriorityHint: Several modes active at once: the highest priority counts (on a tie, the most recent). "Blind" always comes first.
VisionModes.TintHint: Empty = none. A lit item's color replaces it.
VisionModes.DarkHint: Within its range: the scenery stays visible without light.
VisionModes.HeatHint: Heat halo: every visible token carries one, except those hidden from thermal vision (GM button on the sheet, or an effect).
VisionModes.ImportBad: Unreadable file: this is not a vision modes export.
VisionModes.ThroughHint: Number or formula read on the viewer's sheet (scene units). Spots tokens, without seeing the scenery behind walls.
VisionModes.CondHint: Formula read on the watched token's sheet (a value, hasEffect("key")…). Empty = no condition.
VisionModes.TargetsHint: Applies to invisible tokens and what is spotted through walls.

Level.WindowZone: Level-up window: components placed here do not show on the sheet.
Level.ModeHint: Through experience: a level becomes available when XP reaches the threshold. Given levels: no XP, the level comes from a quest reward, a button or the GM.
Level.ThresholdsHint: Total XP to reach the next level: a list ("100, 300, 600" = levels 2, 3, 4…) or a formula where "level" is the current level ("level * 1000").
Level.Button: "Level up" button when a level is available
Level.ComponentHint: The key holds the level (a number, usable in formulas). In the workshop, place inside the component what the level-up window will show.
Level.KeyNeeded: A Level component needs a key (it holds the level).
Level.Commit_live: Right away (the level goes up when the window opens)
Level.CommitHint: "On Validate": choices are written to the sheet as they are made, but closing or cancelling removes them. "Right away": they stay.
Level.BudgetFieldsHint: "strength:1, agility:2": +1 strength costs 1 point, +1 agility costs 2. "level" is the level reached in the points formula.
Level.BudgetMustLabel: "Validate" only when every point is spent
Level.LeftoverKeyHint: Unspent points are added to this sheet key (empty = lost).
Level.WindowEmpty: Nothing to choose for this level.
Level.BudgetMust: Some points are still to spend.
Level.Pending: A level-up request is already waiting for the GM.
Level.GmOnly: Only the GM levels this up.
Level.ReadyGm: Level {n} available (the GM levels it up)
Level.AskNote: {user} asks to level {name} up to {n}: see the chat.
Level.BudgetSellLabel: Allow lowering a field below its opening value (selling back points already owned)
Level.BudgetFloor: Cannot go below the opening value.
Level.AskDownText: {user} asks for {name} to go back down to level {n} ({label}).
Level.AskDownNote: {user} asks for {name} to go down to level {n}.
Level.PendingDownTo: Down to level {n}, waiting for the GM
Level.RulesUpHint: Run on level-up, for the level reached, in order.
Level.DownWho: Who can go down a level
Level.DownUndoHint: Restores the values from before that level-up and takes back the items and effects its rules gave. What a template button did is not undone.
Level.RulesDownHint: Run when going down, for the level left, in order.
Level.ReceivedHint: When a quest or a button gives levels: “Available” shows “Level up” (window, budget, rules, approval); “Right away” applies the levels with the level-up rules, without a window.

Money.Name: Name
Money.Hint: Currencies are used by trades, chests and merchants. Each currency is counted on a character sheet key (a number field). The smallest is worth 1; the others are worth a number of it (1 gold = 100 copper). A single currency is enough if your game has only one.
Money.None: No currency: trades, chests and merchants have no money.
Money.KeyTwice: Two currencies use the same key.
Money.RateTwice: Two currencies have the same value.

Merchant.MenuHint: The game's currencies (trades, chests, merchants) and merchant settings.
Merchant.PriceKeyHint: The item template field holding the price, in base units (the smallest currency). The GM can change an item's price in the shop.
Merchant.Side_sellHint: The item families (templates) merchants can put on sale; exceptions are never sold.
Merchant.Side_buyHint: The item families players can sell back to merchants; exceptions are never bought.
Merchant.LookHint: The token appearance for an open / closed shop is set in Token appearances (“Shop” rule).
Merchant.MarkupHint: Added to the price of every item sold: 30 = +30%, −10 = a 10% discount.
Merchant.CashHint: What the merchant can pay when an item is sold to them, and where the money from their sales goes.
Merchant.BuybackPctHint: A number or a formula on the keys of the item sold (its condition, its rarity…).
Merchant.Rebuy: The seller can buy back what they sold
Merchant.ShopsHint: The base shop is built into the system: nothing to create. For another look, a “shop” template built in the workshop (or a copy of the base shop). Each merchant picks theirs, otherwise the default one.
Merchant.NoShops: No other template: merchants use the built-in base shop.
Merchant.CreateBaseShop: Copy the base shop to edit it
Merchant.DeleteShopUsers: {n} merchant(s) use it: they will switch to the default shop template.
Merchant.ShopModelHint: How their shop looks (“Merchants and currencies” manager, Shops tab).
Merchant.Keep: An item sold by a player
Merchant.Keep_stock: Joins the stock (for sale to everyone)
Merchant.Keep_rebuy: Is kept for the seller to buy back
Merchant.RebuyFormulaHint: A number or a formula on the item's keys.
Merchant.HaggleHint: The % for each outcome, offered when the GM starts a negotiation: positive = in the player's favor (they pay less, get more when selling), negative = the opposite.
Merchant.PlaceHint: Place it on the scene (mouse wheel: rotate). Its settings open next; its stock is filled in its shop.

Shop.Title: Shop
Shop.NoBuyer: No buyer: control a character's token to buy in their place.
Shop.SellDrop: Drop an item from your inventory here to sell it
Shop.SpatialOut: {n} item(s) do not fit in the grid.
Shop.ViewHint: List: number of columns. Grids: cell size; spatial grid: columns and rows (each item's footprint comes from its spatial grid setting).
Shop.Tabs_key: By the value of a key
Shop.TabKeyHint: An item template key (a category, a rarity…): one tab per value.
Shop.TabKeyNeeded: Choose the key that makes the tabs.
Shop.GenreToShopHint: This template will become the look of a shop: it will no longer be used to create characters, and the workshop will offer the Stall, the Till, the Buyer's purse and the Selling zone.
Shop.GenreToCharacterHint: This template will become a character template again: the shop components it holds will no longer show anything.
Shop.NeedCharacter: You need a character (assigned, or a controlled token) to buy.
Shop.TooFar: You are too far from the merchant.
Shop.ClosedBannerPlayer: Shop closed: no buying or selling for now.
Shop.NoPack: Import the item from the compendium into the world first.
Shop.NotSold: Merchants don't sell "{name}" ("Merchants and currencies" manager, Items and prices tab).
Shop.UniqueHint: Unique copy carried by the merchant ({n}). It leaves their sheet when bought.
Shop.PriceHint: Empty: the template's price key. Otherwise a number, or a formula on the item's keys. The merchant's markup is added.
Shop.RestockHint: The quantity goes back up to this number (0 = never). The stall's "Restock" button does it right away.
Shop.SoldOutMsg: This item is no longer available.
Shop.NoGM: No GM connected: buying isn't possible right now.
Shop.Gone: This purchase is no longer possible.
Shop.BoughtAtFeet: Bought: {qty} × {name} for {price}. No room in the inventory: the item is at your feet.
Shop.GmHint: Drop items here · right-click an item to set it up
Shop.NoBuyerSell: No seller: control a character's token to sell on their behalf.
Shop.SellEmpty: Nothing in your inventory that this merchant buys.
Shop.NoBudget: The merchant doesn't have enough money to pay.
Shop.NotYours: This item isn't in your inventory.
Shop.Locked: This item is locked: it can't be sold.
Shop.NotEmpty: Empty this item first: it holds other items.
Shop.AskRebuyText: {user} wants to buy back {name} for {buyer}, price: {price}.
Shop.Until_day: until the end of the day
Shop.HaggleNoRoll: No rollable field in the character templates.
Shop.HaggleNoSide: Tick their purchases, their sales, or both.

Carousel.MenuHint: The strip of combatant portraits: position, size, buttons.
Carousel.PosHint: Each player can change their own with the carousel's button.
Carousel.BtnGmCombat: Combat and turns (start, end, previous / next turn and round)
Carousel.BtnPlayerEnd: "End my turn" on their portrait during their turn
Carousel.BtnPlayerInit: "Roll initiative" on their portrait while they have no score
Carousel.BtnPlayerInitHint: If initiative is rolled automatically (Combat rules → Initiative), the button doesn't show: the score is already there.
Carousel.AnimHint: Portraits sliding when the turn changes, the active combatant lighting up, the round pulsing. "Follow the computer's setting" turns them off when the computer asks for reduced motion.
Carousel.BarsHint: Up to 2 bars at the bottom of each portrait (hit points, energy…). Value and maximum: a sheet key or a formula; a gauge gives its own maximum.
Carousel.EffectsOn: Show the icons of active effects
Carousel.TipWhoHint: What it shows of other characters; the GM always sees everything.
Carousel.NoTipKeys: No values: only the name and effects.
Carousel.ClickPan: Click on a portrait: center the view on the token (and select it if it's yours)
Carousel.ClickPanHint: Never on a token the player can't see.
Carousel.ClickHover: Hovering a portrait: highlight the token
Carousel.ClickHoverHint: The token lights up on the scene as if hovered.
Carousel.ClickSheet: Double-click: open the sheet (if allowed to see it)
Carousel.ClickMenuHint: Right-click (GM): make active, hide / show, defeated, ping, remove from combat.
Carousel.UntilTurn: NPCs hidden from players until their first turn
Carousel.ShownHint: A hidden combatant (eye in the combat tracker) is always invisible to players. What is hidden from players stays visible to the GM, faded.
Carousel.RulesHint: Each rule reads a combatant: a formula that is true on their sheet, or an active effect (its name or status). It hides them from the carousel, marks them defeated, or removes them from combat.
Carousel.ThemeHint: The SBE theme follows the system colors (dark or light per player). A theme of its own has colors for dark and for light.
Carousel.ThemeLiveHint: The displayed carousel changes while you adjust; closing without saving goes back to the saved theme.
Carousel.ThemeImported: Carousel theme imported (save to keep it).
Carousel.ThemeBadFile: This file isn't a carousel theme.
Carousel.ActiveGlow: Animated glow around the active combatant
Carousel.ActiveScaleHint: 100 = same size as the other portraits.
Carousel.MarkNext: “Next” tab on the next combatant to act
Carousel.MarkPlayed: Dim those who already acted this round
Carousel.RoundName: Active combatant's name in the round badge
Carousel.DefeatIconHint: Shown over a defeated combatant's portrait.
Carousel.TipHeader: Header: small portrait, disposition and initiative
Carousel.TipMeters: Small bar under a value that has a maximum
Carousel.AlignHint: When the top carousel isn't full: against the sidebar, or on the left.
Carousel.SettingEnabledHint: Shows the portrait strip during combats. Its settings are in “Combat carousel” above.
Carousel.EnabledWhere: The carousel is turned on with the “Combat carousel” box in the system settings.
Carousel.AdvCssHint: Limited to the carousel and its tooltip (@keyframes allowed). Useful classes: .sbe-car-p (portrait), .sbe-car-img, .sbe-car-shade, .is-active, .is-next, .is-played, .is-defeated, .sbe-car-round, .sbe-car-name, .sbe-car-init, .sbe-car-gauge, .sbe-car-btns, .sbe-car-tip; .is-anim when animations are allowed. A library SVG: var(--svg-name).
Carousel.AdvCssRefused: Carousel CSS refused: it can't be read.
Carousel.AdvSvgsHint: Each SVG becomes var(--svg-name) in your CSS. Paste its code, or choose a world file (the export then only keeps its path). Pasted code wins over the file.

Demo.MenuHint: Installs a ready-to-play village that shows everything the system does: sheets, items, combat, merchants, chests, traps, quests… Removed in one click.
Demo.Title: "Brumeval" demo
Demo.Intro: Brumeval is a small village built entirely with the system: four heroes, locals, creatures, a map with its doors, chest, trap and merchant, a guide and a quest log.
Demo.StateOn: The demo is installed in this world.
Demo.Hint: Removing the demo deletes everything it brought and puts the system settings back as they were before install.
Demo.NoPack: The demo pack cannot be found (restart the world after a system update).
Demo.Already: The demo is already installed: remove it first to reinstall it.
Demo.Installed: The demo is installed: enjoy your visit to Brumeval!
Demo.Failed: Installing the demo failed (details in the console).
Demo.Removed: The demo is removed, the previous settings are back.
Demo.ConflictIntro: The demo brings its own settings. These would replace settings you have changed: tick the ones the demo may replace.
Demo.ConflictHint: An unticked setting stays yours: the part of the demo that uses it may then misbehave. Everything is put back when you remove the demo.
Demo.RemoveBody: {n} demo document(s) will be deleted (scene, sheets, items, journals, table, folders). This cannot be undone.
Demo.RemoveSettings: These settings will get back their value from before the install:

Docs.MenuHint: The full SBE manual: every setting explained with an example. The small book in window headers opens the right page directly.
Docs.Title: SBE documentation
